title: The format page says how records are kept, then indexes kinds, relations and checks
statement: The format page (`?page=format`) MUST say how records are kept, then show an index: the kinds by stage, the relations with their words read both ways, and the checks under Errors and Warnings. Kinds and checks MUST be clickable rows leading to their pages.

title: Format pages open in the wiki card over the stage
statement: Each format page MUST open in the wiki card, the whole page, over the current focus (`?page=format/…`), the stage keeping its focus behind it (a bottom sheet on a phone), with a link back to the focus's own page. Collapsing the card, Escape or moving to another focus MUST close it.

title: A kind page shows everything the reference says about the kind, with a real example
statement: A kind's page (`?page=format/kinds/<kind>`) MUST show its description; its stage; its allowed parents and children as links to their kind pages; its columns, each with its type, whether it is required, its meaning and its own anchor; its obligation, its ID pattern and its ID scope; the relations out of it and into it by their readable labels, each naming the kind at the other end; and the checks that concern it. It MUST show the product's first record of the kind with a link to it, and the count of the product's records of the kind, with a row per parent leading to that parent's group of them.

title: Every kind and every check has one page, from the product's own data
statement: The kinds, relations, folders and checks the reference pages show MUST be the product's own: the schema with its product kinds, and Lathe's check rows with the product's. The pages MUST be built from the loaded data; a check that reports problems but has no row is the engine's own, listed without an explanation. Each kind MUST have one page at `?page=format/kinds/<kind>` and each check one page at `?page=format/checks/<check>`, on whatever focus the stage shows, named by the kind's or check's name as records and problems carry it. A name the format does not know MUST say so, with a link to the format page.

title: A check page shows its explanation, its query and the problems it reports now
statement: A check's page (`?page=format/checks/<check>`) MUST show its severity, its summary and explanation (rendered Markdown), where it comes from and its query, the kinds it concerns, and the current space's problems with that code as clickable rows.

title: The check page reads a check through the Check aggregate's own query
statement: A check page MUST read a check that has a row, Lathe's or the product's own, through the Check aggregate's own query, `GET /api/check/get-check?name=<name>`, and draw its summary, explanation, severity, where it comes from, its place in the run order, its query and the kinds it concerns from that answer. A check the engine reports itself has no row, and its page says so.

title: The check page writes only through the Check aggregate's commands, one per change
statement: A check page MUST change data only when the Owner acts on a product's own check, and then only by sending one of the Check aggregate's own commands, `POST /api/check/<command>`: Edit sends Change a check with only what changed (emptied kinds as null), and Remove sends Remove a check after asking. A check is added from the record format's Checks with Add a check, for the product of the current space. Lathe's own checks are read-only, so their page offers no actions; the aggregate has no Move.

title: A refused Check command keeps the draft and shows why
statement: When a Check command is refused, its form or question MUST stay open with what the Owner entered, show every reason the command gave at its top in the rule's own words, and take focus to them; nothing on the page and no data file changes.

title: The Changes panel lists the changes newest first, by record, as cards
statement: The Changes panel MUST list the records changed since the baseline, newest first (those that changed while the page was open by when they landed, then the rest by ID), by record, each a card naming its kind, ID and title, what changed and when, and its fields old → new. Clicking a card MUST focus its record on the stage, the panel staying open with that card marked; a removed record's card MUST show what it was instead, since it has no page.

title: Its toggle shows how many records changed
statement: The Changes panel's toggle, among every stage's Changes controls, MUST show how many records changed since the baseline, and its accessible name MUST say it in words.

title: The page reads its use case whole through the aggregate's own query
statement: A Use case page MUST read the use case that holds its record whole through the Use case aggregate's own query, `GET /api/use-case/get-use-case?id=<ID>`, by the ID of any record in it, and draw what that record holds of it from that answer, never from a generic record read; it MUST read it again whenever the data is read again, keeping what it last read on screen meanwhile.

title: The page writes only through the Use case aggregate's commands, one per change
statement: A Use case page MUST change data only when the Owner acts on its record actions, and then only by sending one of the Use case aggregate's own commands, `POST /api/use-case/<command>`: Edit sends its kind's Change with only what changed, Add (a kind that sits under the record in the use case, with the next free ID read through `next-id`) its kind's Add, Move (a use case only) Move a use case, as its own action, and Remove its kind's Remove after naming what goes with the record. A use case is added from its capability's page through Add a use case.

title: A refused command shows every reason, keeps what was entered and changes nothing
statement: When a Use case command is refused, its form or question MUST stay open with what the Owner entered, show every reason the command gave at its top in the rule's own words, without a file and line, and take focus to them; nothing on the page and no data file changes, and the Owner can fix the input and send it again.

title: Steps are shown in their positions, as numbers
statement: A flow's steps MUST be shown in their `position`, compared as numbers (so step 10 comes after step 2), then by ID; the store refuses a step without a whole-number position, so none is ever hidden.

title: A step is always shown under its flow
statement: Wherever steps are shown, on a page or in the graph, each MUST be shown under the flow it belongs to, never as a record apart from it.

title: A flow's page shows its steps in order as a table
statement: A flow's record page MUST show its steps, when it has any, as a table in step order with the columns Step (order and ID), What happens (the title), Invokes, Fulfills and Exchanges with, each linked ID going to its record, and a variant step naming the one interface that does it. Where the page is too narrow for every column, as in the wiki card, each step MUST be laid out stacked instead: its number and ID on one line, What happens wrapping at full width beneath, and each link column below under its name, so no text is drawn cut, scrolled out of sight or squeezed to a word per line.

title: A step's linked titles fold under its row
statement: Each step row MUST show one level: the step and the IDs it links to. The titles and kinds of what it invokes, exchanges with and fulfills MUST be folded under the row's disclosure, with Expand all and Collapse all for the table; a step has no text beyond its title.

title: A step row shows its problems, and a flow without steps shows no table
statement: A step's row MUST carry a badge for its errors or warnings. A flow with no steps MUST NOT show a steps table.

title: A flow with several paths shows a table per path
statement: When a flow's steps sit on more than one `path` (a step with no path is on the main path), its page MUST show each path as its own table, headed by the path's name, the main path first and then the others by name, each in its own step order, never interleaved by `position` across paths.

title: A use case shows its requirements in a table
statement: A use case's Traceability MUST show a table with one row per UC requirement and the columns Requirement, Designed, Built and Proved, each cell linking the records that design, build or prove it and flagging a gap, followed by its flow and the patterns it follows. Where the page is too narrow for every column, as in the wiki card, each requirement MUST be laid out stacked instead: the requirement on one line and Designed, Built and Proved beneath it under their names, so no text is drawn cut or scrolled out of sight.

title: A use case shows its flow and the interfaces that offer it
statement: A use case's page MUST show its flow, as a link, and list the interfaces that offer it by ID, each a link with its kind when its name does not say it.

title: A flow's page has a tab per interface that offers its use case
statement: A flow's page MUST show a tablist: All interfaces first, the flow as written and the only place it is edited, then one tab per interface that offers its use case, by ID, each showing that interface's version of the flow, derived: its actor, the patterns it follows and their rules, and its steps without the other interfaces' variants, each with where it is carried out as links, and a step the interface cannot reach as a gap. The arrow keys, Home and End MUST move between the tabs.

title: The page reads its record through the Business outcome aggregate's own query
statement: A Business outcome page MUST read its record through the Business outcome aggregate's own query, `GET /api/business-outcome/get-business-outcome?id=<ID>`, and draw it from that answer, never from a generic record read; it MUST read it again whenever the data is read again, keeping what it last read on screen meanwhile.

title: The page writes only through the Business outcome aggregate's commands, one per change
statement: A Business outcome page MUST change data only when the Owner acts on its record actions, and then only by sending one of the Business outcome aggregate's own commands, `POST /api/business-outcome/<command>`: Edit sends Change a business outcome with only what changed, and Remove sends Remove a business outcome; the aggregate has no Move. An outcome is added from its product's page through Add a business outcome, with the next free ID read through `next-id`.

title: A refused Business outcome command shows every reason and changes nothing
statement: When a Business outcome command is refused, its form or question MUST stay open with what the Owner entered, show every reason the command gave at its top in the rule's own words, without a file and line, and take focus to them; nothing on the page and no data file changes, and the Owner can fix the input and send it again.

title: An outcome's page shows what measures it
statement: A business outcome's page MUST list the tests and records that measure it under Measured by, and how it is measured outside the code when it says so.

title: The page reads its record through the Extension record aggregate's own query
statement: A Extension record page MUST read its record through the Extension record aggregate's own query, `GET /api/extension-record/get-extension-record?id=<ID>`, and draw it from that answer, never from a generic record read; it MUST read it again whenever the data is read again, keeping what it last read on screen meanwhile.

title: The page writes only through the Extension record aggregate's commands, one per change
statement: A Extension record page MUST change data only when the Owner acts on its record actions, and then only by sending one of the Extension record aggregate's own commands, `POST /api/extension-record/<command>`: Edit sends Change an extension record with only the declared values, links and packages that changed, and Remove sends Remove an extension record; the aggregate has no Move. A record is added from its parent's page through Add an extension record, its fields those its kind declares.

title: A refused Extension record command shows every reason and changes nothing
statement: When a Extension record command is refused, its form or question MUST stay open with what the Owner entered, show every reason the command gave at its top in the rule's own words, without a file and line, and take focus to them; nothing on the page and no data file changes, and the Owner can fix the input and send it again.

title: The page reads its record through the Entry point aggregate's own query
statement: A Entry point page MUST read its record through the Entry point aggregate's own query, `GET /api/entry-point/get-entry-point?id=<ID>`, and draw it from that answer, never from a generic record read; it MUST read it again whenever the data is read again, keeping what it last read on screen meanwhile.

title: The page writes only through the Entry point aggregate's commands, one per change
statement: A Entry point page MUST change data only when the Owner acts on its record actions, and then only by sending one of the Entry point aggregate's own commands, `POST /api/entry-point/<command>`: Edit sends Change an entry point with only what changed, and Remove sends Remove an entry point; the aggregate has no Move. An entry point is added from its domain's page through Add an entry point, with the next free ID read through `next-id`.

title: A refused Entry point command shows every reason and changes nothing
statement: When a Entry point command is refused, its form or question MUST stay open with what the Owner entered, show every reason the command gave at its top in the rule's own words, without a file and line, and take focus to them; nothing on the page and no data file changes, and the Owner can fix the input and send it again.

title: The page reads its record through the Tooling aggregate's own query
statement: A Tooling page MUST read its record through the Tooling aggregate's own query, `GET /api/tooling/get-tooling?id=<ID>`, and draw it from that answer, never from a generic record read; it MUST read it again whenever the data is read again, keeping what it last read on screen meanwhile.

title: The page writes only through the Tooling aggregate's commands, one per change
statement: A Tooling page MUST change data only when the Owner acts on its record actions, and then only by sending one of the Tooling aggregate's own commands, `POST /api/tooling/<command>`: Edit sends Change a tooling record with only what changed (an emptied file cleared), and Remove sends Remove a tooling record; the aggregate has no Move. A tooling record is added from its domain's page through Add a tooling record, with the next free ID read through `next-id`.

title: A refused Tooling command shows every reason and changes nothing
statement: When a Tooling command is refused, its form or question MUST stay open with what the Owner entered, show every reason the command gave at its top in the rule's own words, without a file and line, and take focus to them; nothing on the page and no data file changes, and the Owner can fix the input and send it again.

title: The page reads its domain through the aggregate's own query
statement: A Domain records page MUST read the domain that holds its record through the Domain aggregate's own query, `GET /api/domain/get-domain?id=<ID>`, by the ID of any record in it, and draw what that record holds of it from that answer, never from a generic record read.

title: The page writes only through the Domain aggregate's commands, one per change
statement: A Domain records page MUST change data only when the Owner acts on its record actions, and then only by sending one of the Domain aggregate's own commands, `POST /api/domain/<command>`: Edit sends its kind's Change with only what changed (an emptied field the command may clear as null), Add sends the Add of a kind that sits under the record with the next free ID read from the aggregate, and Remove sends its kind's Remove after saying what goes with it. The aggregate has no Move command, so the page offers no Move.

title: A refused Domain command keeps the draft and shows why
statement: When a Domain command is refused, its form or question MUST stay open with what the Owner entered, show every reason the command gave at its top in the rule's own words, and take focus to them; nothing on the page and no data file changes.

title: A capability lists the outcomes it serves and its use cases
statement: A capability's page MUST list the business outcomes it serves (in its Traceability, under Serves) and its use cases, in a section with their count.

title: The page reads its test data set through the aggregate's own query
statement: A Test data set page MUST read the test data set that holds its record through the Test data set aggregate's own query, `GET /api/test-data-set/get-test-data-set?id=<ID>`, and draw what that record holds of it from that answer, never from a generic record read.

title: The page writes only through the Test data set aggregate's commands, one per change
statement: A Test data set page MUST change data only when the Owner acts on its record actions, and then only by sending one of the Test data set aggregate's own commands, `POST /api/test-data-set/<command>`: Edit sends its kind's Change with only what changed (an emptied field the command may clear as null), Add sends the Add of a kind that sits under the record with the next free ID read from the aggregate, and Remove sends its kind's Remove after saying what goes with it. The aggregate has no Move command, so the page offers no Move.

title: A refused Test data set command keeps the draft and shows why
statement: When a Test data set command is refused, its form or question MUST stay open with what the Owner entered, show every reason the command gave at its top in the rule's own words, and take focus to them; nothing on the page and no data file changes.

title: A test data set shows its setup and the tests that start from it
statement: A test data set's page MUST show its description, its environment, accounts, starting records, how to prepare and reset it, and the tests that start from it (in its Traceability, under Starting point of).

title: The page reads its pattern through the aggregate's own query
statement: A Pattern page MUST read the pattern that holds its record through the Pattern aggregate's own query, `GET /api/pattern/get-pattern?id=<ID>`, by the ID of any record in it, and draw what that record holds of it from that answer, never from a generic record read.

title: The page writes only through the Pattern aggregate's commands, one per change
statement: A Pattern page MUST change data only when the Owner acts on its record actions, and then only by sending one of the Pattern aggregate's own commands, `POST /api/pattern/<command>`: Edit sends its kind's Change with only what changed (an emptied field the command may clear as null), Add sends the Add of a kind that sits under the record with the next free ID read from the aggregate, and Remove sends its kind's Remove after saying what goes with it. The aggregate has no Move command, so the page offers no Move.

title: A refused Pattern command keeps the draft and shows why
statement: When a Pattern command is refused, its form or question MUST stay open with what the Owner entered, show every reason the command gave at its top in the rule's own words, and take focus to them; nothing on the page and no data file changes.

title: A pattern page shows its settings, rules and followers
statement: A pattern's page (`/<id>`) MUST show a settings table (each setting, what it means and the rules that depend on it), its rules, and each domain that follows it with that domain's following use cases, the value each gives for each setting, and the domain's status for each rule as on the domain page. A pattern nobody follows MUST say that no domain owes its rules. The rules MUST NOT be listed a second time as plain children.

title: A pattern rule page shows the domains that owe it
statement: A pattern rule's page MUST list each domain that follows its pattern, all of which owe the rule, with whether that domain proves it: proved, not automated yet or not proved.

title: Followed by and Owed by read the followers through the Pattern following aggregate's own query
statement: A pattern's Followed by and a rule's Owed by MUST read the pattern's followers through the Pattern following aggregate's own query, `GET /api/pattern-following/list-followers?pattern_id=<ID>`: each domain that follows the pattern, whether the domain itself does, and each of its use cases that does, with the value or the reason it does not apply each gives each setting. Each rule's standing in a domain is the coverage's.

title: The following's editor writes only through the Pattern following aggregate's commands, one per change
statement: The followers MUST change only when the Owner acts on a follower's row or on Follow, and then only by sending one of the Pattern following aggregate's own commands, `POST /api/pattern-following/<command>`: Change values sends Change the setting values with the whole list, only when it changed; Stop following asks first and sends Stop following a pattern; Follow sends Follow a pattern for a domain or use case of the pattern's product that does not follow it yet, with a row for each of its settings.

title: A refused Pattern following command keeps the draft and shows why
statement: When a Pattern following command is refused, its form MUST stay open with what the Owner entered, show every reason the command gave at its top in the rule's own words, and take focus to them; nothing on the page and no data file changes.

title: The page reads its standard through the aggregate's own query
statement: A Standard page MUST read the standard that holds its record through the Standard aggregate's own query, `GET /api/standard/get-standard?id=<ID>`, by the ID of any record in it, and draw what that record holds of it from that answer, never from a generic record read.

title: The page writes only through the Standard aggregate's commands, one per change
statement: A Standard page MUST change data only when the Owner acts on its record actions, and then only by sending one of the Standard aggregate's own commands, `POST /api/standard/<command>`: Edit sends its kind's Change with only what changed (an emptied field the command may clear as null), Add sends the Add of a kind that sits under the record with the next free ID read from the aggregate, and Remove sends its kind's Remove after saying what goes with it. The aggregate has no Move command, so the page offers no Move.

title: A refused Standard command keeps the draft and shows why
statement: When a Standard command is refused, its form or question MUST stay open with what the Owner entered, show every reason the command gave at its top in the rule's own words, and take focus to them; nothing on the page and no data file changes.

title: A standard lists its rules with what meets each one and its tests
statement: A standard's page MUST list its rules in a table, one row each under their groups, with what meets each rule and the standard rule tests that prove it, and say when nothing does yet.

title: A standard rule shows what meets it and its tests
statement: A standard rule's Traceability MUST list what meets it under Met by and its standard rule tests under Proved by, and what meets it MUST list the rule under Meets. The reference MUST have a page for each standard kind, made from the schema.

title: A refused Aggregate command keeps the draft and shows why
statement: When a Aggregate command is refused, its form or question MUST stay open with what the Owner entered, show every reason the command gave at its top in the rule's own words, and take focus to them; nothing on the page and no data file changes.

title: An aggregate lists its domain events with what raises and hears them
statement: An aggregate's page MUST list its domain events in their own list titled "Domain events", each row one link to the event saying whether it is published, which commands raise it and how many policies hear it, in the relations' own words from the schema.

title: Each record shows what it holds of its aggregate
statement: An aggregate's page MUST show the aggregate's identity, entities and invariants; an entity's page its fields with their types, its data model and the commands that change it; an invariant's page its rule and its test.

title: Each record offers the changes its aggregate allows
statement: Each record of an aggregate MUST offer Edit, Add for what may sit under it (an entity, an invariant or a domain event under the aggregate, an entity's one data model, an invariant's one rule and one test, each only while there is room for it) and Remove, which says what goes with it first. A domain event or command is added from the aggregate's or the entity's page. Nothing in an aggregate MUST be offered a Move: a record stays in its aggregate.

title: A refused Domain event command keeps the draft and shows why
statement: When a Domain event command is refused, its form or question MUST stay open with what the Owner entered, show every reason the command gave at its top in the rule's own words, and take focus to them; nothing on the page and no data file changes.

title: An event shows its fields and what raises and hears it
statement: A domain event's page MUST show its fields as an entity's page shows its fields, and its Traceability MUST list "Raised by" and "Heard by", in the relations' own words from the schema.

title: Domain event page offers the changes its aggregate allows
statement: Each record of a domain event MUST offer Edit, Add an event type for an event that has none, and Remove, which says what goes with it. A domain event is added from its aggregate's page. Nothing MUST be offered a Move: a record stays in its aggregate.

title: A refused Command command keeps the draft and shows why
statement: When a Command command is refused, its form or question MUST stay open with what the Owner entered, show every reason the command gave at its top in the rule's own words, and take focus to them; nothing on the page and no data file changes.

title: A command lists its handler, policies and endpoints
statement: A command's page MUST list its handler, its policies and the endpoints that expose it, each in its own section with its count, each endpoint's row with its method and route.

title: A policy lists the event it hears
statement: A policy's Traceability MUST list the event it hears under "Hears", in the relation's own words from the schema.

title: Command page offers the changes its aggregate allows
statement: Each record of a command MUST offer Edit, Add for what may sit under it (the command's one handler or a policy; a policy's one event handler and one test) and Remove, which says what goes with it. A command is added from its entity's page. Nothing MUST be offered a Move: a record stays in its aggregate.

title: A refused Table command keeps the draft and shows why
statement: When a Table command is refused, its form or question MUST stay open with what the Owner entered, show every reason the command gave at its top in the rule's own words, and take focus to them; nothing on the page and no data file changes.

title: A table lists its keys in order with what each enforces, references or holds where
statement: A table's page MUST list its keys and indexes in order in a table, one row each with its name (or unnamed), its type and its columns, a unique key with the invariant it enforces and its condition, and a foreign key with the table it references; and say when it has none.

title: Table page offers the changes its aggregate allows
statement: Each record of a table MUST offer Edit, Add for what may sit under it, and Remove, which says what goes with it. A table also offers Move, to another entity, read model or domain of its product, as its own action. A table is added from the page it sits under.

title: A refused Specification command keeps the draft and shows why
statement: When a Specification command is refused, its form or question MUST stay open with what the Owner entered, show every reason the command gave at its top in the rule's own words, and take focus to them; nothing on the page and no data file changes.

title: A specification shows its predicate and its test, or that they are not written yet
statement: A specification's page MUST show its statement, then its predicate and its test, each as a row leading to it or saying it is not written yet; the aggregates it reads are among its links.

title: Specification page offers the changes its aggregate allows
statement: Each record of a specification MUST offer Edit, Add for what may sit under it, and Remove, which says what goes with it. A specification is added from the page it sits under. Nothing MUST be offered a Move: a record stays in its aggregate.

title: A refused Value object command keeps the draft and shows why
statement: When a Value object command is refused, its form or question MUST stay open with what the Owner entered, show every reason the command gave at its top in the rule's own words, and take focus to them; nothing on the page and no data file changes.

title: A value object shows its fields, its constraints with their tests, and its value type
statement: A value object's page MUST show its description, its fields in order as a table with each one's meaning, type and whether it is required, its constraints as a table with the test that proves each (or Nothing yet), and its value type or that it is not written yet; a constraint test's page MUST show what it accepts and what it refuses.

title: Value object page offers the changes its aggregate allows
statement: Each record of a value object MUST offer Edit, Add for what may sit under it, and Remove, which says what goes with it. A value object is added from the page it sits under. Nothing MUST be offered a Move: a record stays in its aggregate.

title: A refused Read model command keeps the draft and shows why
statement: When a Read model command is refused, its form or question MUST stay open with what the Owner entered, show every reason the command gave at its top in the rule's own words, and take focus to them; nothing on the page and no data file changes.

title: A read model shows its fields, queries with handlers, projection and reader
statement: A read model's page MUST show its description, its fields in order as a table with their types, its queries as a table with each one's handler (or Nothing yet), and its projection and its reader, each as a row leading to it or saying it is not written yet; what it reads, calls and is fed by are among its links.

title: Read model page offers the changes its aggregate allows
statement: Each record of a read model MUST offer Edit, Add for what may sit under it, and Remove, which says what goes with it. A read model is added from the page it sits under. Nothing MUST be offered a Move: a record stays in its aggregate.

title: A refused View command keeps the draft and shows why
statement: When a View command is refused, its form or question MUST stay open with what the Owner entered, show every reason the command gave at its top in the rule's own words, and take focus to them; nothing on the page and no data file changes.

title: A view lists its requirements under their groups with their tests
statement: A view's page MUST list its view requirements in a table, one row each under their groups (the ungrouped ones first), with the view tests that prove each one, and say when nothing does yet.

title: View page offers the changes its aggregate allows
statement: Each record of a view MUST offer Edit, Add for what may sit under it, and Remove, which says what goes with it. A view is added from its product's page, with no parent. Nothing MUST be offered a Move: a record stays in its aggregate.

title: A refused UI component command keeps the draft and shows why
statement: When a UI component command is refused, its form or question MUST stay open with what the Owner entered, show every reason the command gave at its top in the rule's own words, and take focus to them; nothing on the page and no data file changes.

title: A UI component shows its description and the packages it uses
statement: A UI component's page MUST show its description and the packages it uses, and in its Traceability the views it renders.

title: UI component page offers the changes its aggregate allows
statement: A UI component MUST offer Edit and Remove, which asks first. A UI component is added from its product's page. Nothing MUST be offered a Move: a record stays in its aggregate.

title: A refused Endpoint command keeps the draft and shows why
statement: When an Endpoint command is refused, its form or question MUST stay open with what the Owner entered, show every reason the command gave at its top in the rule's own words, and take focus to them; nothing on the page and no data file changes.

title: An endpoint lists its API requirements with their count and their tests
statement: An endpoint's page MUST list its API requirements in a section with their count, in a table, one row each under their groups (the ungrouped ones first), with the endpoint tests that prove each one, and say when nothing does yet.

title: An endpoint shows its description and its handler
statement: An endpoint's page MUST show the text of any record in it, an API requirement or the endpoint, and the endpoint's handler.

title: Endpoint page offers the changes its aggregate allows
statement: Each record of an endpoint MUST offer Edit, Add for what may sit under it (an API requirement or, while it has none, the handler under the endpoint; an endpoint test under an API requirement) and Remove, which says what goes with it. The endpoint alone also offers Move, to another command or query of its domain. An endpoint is added from its command's or query's page.

title: A refused Integration command keeps the draft and shows why
statement: When an Integration command is refused, its form or question MUST stay open with what the Owner entered, show every reason the command gave at its top in the rule's own words, and take focus to them; nothing on the page and no data file changes.

title: An integration's page lists its exchanges and names its system
statement: An integration's page MUST list the flow steps that exchange with it, in a section with its count, saying which outside system it is when it names one.

title: An integration shows its adapter and its tests
statement: An integration's page MUST show its adapter and its tests section, and the text of any record in it.

title: Integration page offers the changes its aggregate allows
statement: Each record of an integration MUST offer Edit, Add for what may sit under it (its adapter, while it has none, or an integration test) and Remove, which says what goes with it. An integration is added from its product's page. Nothing MUST be offered a Move: a record stays in its aggregate.

title: A storage requirement's records offer the changes their aggregate allows
statement: Each record of a storage requirement MUST offer Edit, Add for what may sit under it (a test) and Remove, which says what goes with it first. A storage requirement is added from the page of the aggregate or read model it is about through its own Add, and a test from the requirement's page.

title: A refused Storage requirement command keeps the draft and shows why
statement: When a Storage requirement command is refused, its form or question MUST stay open with what the Owner entered, show every reason the command gave at its top in the rule's own words, and take focus to them; nothing on the page and no data file changes.

title: A storage requirement's page names what builds it and where it is kept
statement: A storage requirement's page MUST name, as links, the aggregate or read model it is about, the repository or reader that builds it and the data store that one is stored in, and MUST say so when its aggregate has no repository or its read model no reader yet, or when that one names no data store.

title: A data store's records offer the changes their aggregate allows
statement: A data store MUST offer Edit, Add for what may sit under it, and Remove, which says what goes with it first. A data store is added from the page of the product or domain it sits under through its own Add.

title: A refused Data store command keeps the draft and shows why
statement: When a Data store command is refused, its form or question MUST stay open with what the Owner entered, show every reason the command gave at its top in the rule's own words, and take focus to them; nothing on the page and no data file changes.

title: A data store's page lists what is stored in it and names what provides it
statement: A data store's page MUST list the repositories, readers and tables stored in it, in one section with its count (saying when nothing is stored in it yet), and name among its facts its kind, the product or domain it sits under, and the integration that provides it when one does; its Traceability MUST NOT list them again.

title: The Checks panel lists its product's problems, errors first, grouped by check
statement: The Checks panel MUST list every problem of its space's product, errors before warnings, grouped by check, then the problems that belong to no product (data the store refuses, a check that could not run) under a Workspace heading, which every space's panel shows. It MUST NOT list another product's problems. Selecting a problem MUST focus its record on the stage, which the wiki card then shows, while the panel stays open with that record's rows marked, to work down the list. A problem that names no record MUST open its check's page in the wiki card instead.

title: A problem's code leads to its check
statement: Wherever a problem's check code is shown, in the Checks panel and on a record's page, it MUST be a link that opens that check's page in the wiki card.

title: Each space has its own Checks panel
statement: The Checks panel MUST list the current space's problems only, opened over the stage from the nav's Tools and by the Checks shortcuts (`?panel=checks`), and stay open, showing the new space's problems, when the Reader moves to another focus or space; there MUST be no Checks list for every product at once.

title: The product page shows each domain with its coverage
statement: The product page MUST show each domain as a card that opens the domain page wherever it is clicked, with one group of small bars per obligation kind the engine reports for it, labeled with the kind's label and in the engine's order, each with designed, built, proved and not-automated-yet counts. It MUST NOT name obligation kinds of its own, and a count the engine does not report MUST NOT be shown as zero.

title: The product page lists its open questions and problems
statement: The product page MUST list the product's open questions, with their owners, and the problems found in its records.

title: The product page sums up what Lathe counts across the product
statement: The product page MUST show, in a Summary section, what Lathe counts across the product's domains: designed, built and proved, totaled over every obligation kind; the not-automated-yet count on its own line, apart from proved; a Tests row totaling its domains' tests by state; its open questions; and its errors and warnings. A product with nothing to count MUST show zeros, not an empty section.

title: Each domain card shows its tests by state
statement: Each domain card MUST show the domain's tests by state under its bars, such as `Tests 12 automated, 1 manual, 2 not automated yet`, from `Coverage.tests`.

title: The product page lists its business outcomes first
statement: The product page MUST list its business outcomes before its domains, in the discovery stage's color, each a card that opens the outcome wherever it is clicked, with its statement, measure and target and the capabilities that serve it, saying so when none does; Shared MUST NOT list them again.

title: The page and the nav read the products through the Product aggregate's own queries
statement: A Product page MUST read the product that holds its record through the Product aggregate's own query, `GET /api/product/get-product?id=<ID>`, by the ID of the product, an open question or an interface in it, and draw what that record holds from that answer; the nav's space rail and the products picker MUST list the products through `GET /api/product/list-products`. Each reads again whenever the data is read again, keeping what it last read on screen meanwhile.

title: The page writes only through the Product aggregate's commands, one per change
statement: A Product page MUST change data only when the Owner acts on its record actions, and then only by sending one of the Product aggregate's own commands, `POST /api/product/<command>`: Edit sends its kind's Change with only what changed (a product's roles as one list), Add an open question's or an interface's Add with the next free ID read through `next-id` (an open question under a domain is added the same way from the domain's page), Declare and each declaration's Change and Remove the product kind's or relation's own command, Move (an open question only) Move a question, as its own action, and Remove its kind's Remove. A product has no Remove. Any other record under the product is added through its own aggregate's Add form.

title: A refused Product command shows every reason and changes nothing
statement: When a Product command is refused, its form or question MUST stay open with what the Owner entered, show every reason the command gave at its top in the rule's own words, without a file and line, and take focus to them; nothing on the page and no data file changes, and the Owner can fix the input and send it again.

title: An interface lists its roles, its patterns and the use cases it offers
statement: An interface's page MUST show the roles that use it and the patterns it follows, and list the use cases it offers under their capabilities, in the capabilities' order, then the product's use cases it does not offer.

title: The Limits section reads the product's limits through the Product setting aggregate's own query
statement: A product's page MUST show its Limits, the most children of one kind a record should hold and the most entities an aggregate should hold, read through the Product setting aggregate's own query, `GET /api/product-setting/get-limits?product_id=<ID>`, and say whether the product set them or takes the defaults.

title: Set limits writes only through the Product setting aggregate's command
statement: The Limits section MUST change the product's limits only when the Owner acts on Set limits, and then only by sending the Product setting aggregate's own command, `POST /api/product-setting/set-limits`, with both limits, the form starting at the ones the product has now.

title: A refused Set limits keeps the draft and shows why
statement: When Set limits is refused, its form MUST stay open with what the Owner entered, show every reason the command gave at its top in the rule's own words, and take focus to them; nothing on the page and no data file changes.

title: An open page loads the data again when it changes, at the same address
statement: When the server sends `spec:changed`, an open page MUST load the data again without a manual refresh, staying at the same address.
group_name: Workbench

title: A panel's edge resizes it by drag or keyboard
statement: The inner edge of each resizable floating panel (the navigation and the wiki card) MUST be a handle that resizes it when dragged, and when focused MUST step with the arrow keys (bigger steps with Shift) and jump to the limits with Home and End, the arrow toward the panel shrinking it. Each size MUST stay within its limits: the navigation 256 to 560 px and the wiki card 360 to 900 px.
group_name: Workbench

title: Sizes are remembered, and double-click resets one
statement: Each panel's size MUST be remembered (the navigation's across visits, the wiki card's for the session), a remembered size outside its limits MUST fall back to the default, and double-clicking a handle MUST reset its panel to the default: the navigation 336 px, the wiki card a third of the open space.
group_name: Workbench

title: Dragging the navigation small folds it
statement: Dragging the navigation below 180 px MUST fold it to its rail; dragging the rail's gap out again MUST unfold the navigation. On a narrow screen there MUST be no gaps to drag: the navigation is a sheet.
group_name: Workbench

title: Hiding a panel gives its space to the stage and loses nothing
statement: Hiding the nav or the wiki card MUST give its space to the stage, which frames the focus again in the open space it leaves, and MUST keep a control that brings it back: the nav keeps its rail, and the wiki card's toggle sits at the right of the page bar, as VS Code's layout toggles do, never as a full-height strip. The wiki card and the header strip MUST describe the same page whichever stage shows, so hiding a panel never hides the record's facts for good.
group_name: Workbench

title: A theme applies at once and before first paint
statement: Choosing a theme or a mode MUST apply at once, without a reload. On load, the chosen theme and mode MUST be on the page before the first paint, so it never flashes another theme.
group_name: Workbench

title: One keymap table drives the keys, the palette and the sheet
statement: Every keyboard command MUST be one row in one table (command id, title, group, default keys, where it applies), and the key handlers, the command palette and the shortcuts sheet MUST all be drawn from it, so nothing is listed twice. "Mod" MUST mean Cmd on macOS and Ctrl elsewhere, in matching and in what the app shows (⌘⇧P on a Mac, Ctrl+Shift+P elsewhere).
group_name: Keyboard

title: The default shortcuts follow VS Code
statement: The defaults MUST be: Cmd/Ctrl+P and Cmd/Ctrl+K quick open; Cmd/Ctrl+Shift+P the command palette; Cmd/Ctrl+B the nav; Enter and Ctrl+W (Alt+W off a Mac) to show or collapse the wiki card, and Escape to collapse it (`LA-V96-R19`); Ctrl+G (Alt+G) or Ctrl+1, Ctrl+E (Alt+E) or Ctrl+2, and Ctrl+T (Alt+T) or Ctrl+3 the Graph, ERD and Trace stages; Escape to clear or close the innermost thing; Ctrl+- and Ctrl+Shift+- back and forward (Alt+Left and Alt+Right left to the browser); F12 open the focused link's record; Shift+F12 the wiki card's whole page, with focus moved to its incoming links; Cmd/Ctrl+Shift+M Checks; F8 and Shift+F8 the next and previous problem on the page; Cmd/Ctrl+Shift+E focus the nav; `/` the nearest search box; `?` and Cmd/Ctrl+/ the shortcuts sheet; on the graph `+` and `-` depth, `v` the other of the Tree and Nested layouts, `.` fit, the arrow keys, or W, A, S and D as Up, Left, Down and Right, to step through the tree (Left out and Right in in the Tree layout, Up out and Down in in the Nested layout, the other two across; `LA-V93-R19`) and Enter to focus the box with keyboard focus (on the focus's own box, the wiki card); and `g` then `c`, `f` or `h` for Checks, the format and home, with a small hint while the second key is awaited.
group_name: Keyboard

title: Shortcuts never get in the way of typing or of the browser
statement: Single-key shortcuts MUST NOT fire while typing; the app MUST call preventDefault only for keys it handles (so Cmd/Ctrl+P never opens the print dialog, and unhandled keys reach the browser); and no binding MUST take a browser essential. A shortcut without Ctrl, Cmd or Alt (a letter, a symbol, a sequence such as `g c`) MUST NOT fire while focus is in a text input, a text area, a select or editable text. A plain Enter MUST stay with a control that handles Enter itself, and Escape with a text field. Alt+Left and Alt+Right still go back and forward.
group_name: Keyboard

title: A person can change every shortcut's keys
statement: Every shortcut the app handles itself, the stage walk's included, MUST be customizable in the shortcuts sheet: choosing one of its keys records a new key in its place (the next key pressed with its modifiers; Escape cancels), Add key records one more, and each key can be removed. A changed shortcut MUST show Reset, and the sheet MUST have Reset all, which asks first. The keys are the person's Key bindings (LA-PLT-A14), kept in this browser; the browser's own keys (Alt+Left) and an ARIA control's (a tree's arrows) are shown as fixed.
group_name: Keyboard

title: Every command works without a mouse and is announced
statement: Every command MUST be reachable from the keyboard, and a command that changes what shows (a stage switch, a panel shown or hidden, the next problem) MUST be announced to screen readers through a polite live region.
group_name: Keyboard

title: A command's keys suit the platform
statement: A command MAY have other keys off a Mac. On a Mac, Ctrl means the Control key, so Ctrl+W leaves Cmd+W to the browser; elsewhere Ctrl+W closes the tab, Ctrl+G finds the next match and Ctrl+T opens a tab, so the wiki card and the stages take Alt+W, Alt+G, Alt+E and Alt+T there. In the desktop app Cmd or Ctrl+W and T belong to the menu's Close Tab and New Tab (`LA-V96-R17`). A key reserved for the browser or the system MUST never be offered, even as a person's binding (LA-PLT-INV41), and tooltips, `aria-keyshortcuts`, the command palette and the shortcuts sheet MUST show the keys for the current platform.
group_name: Keyboard

title: A tooltip shows the control and its keys
statement: Every icon button and control that has a shortcut MUST show it in its tooltip as its name then its keys ("Show or hide the navigation ⌘B", or "Ctrl+B" off a Mac), after a short hover delay and at once on keyboard focus.
group_name: Keyboard

title: A control with a shortcut has aria-keyshortcuts
statement: Every control with a shortcut MUST carry `aria-keyshortcuts` with its keys.
group_name: Keyboard

title: Every hint reads from the keymap
statement: Every shortcut hint (tooltip, toolbar button and its key letter, palette row, sheet row, `aria-keyshortcuts`, placeholder, live announcement, and the desktop menu's key labels) MUST be read from the one keymap with the person's keys, so a rebinding changes every hint at once; no hint is written by hand.
group_name: Keyboard

title: A tooltip never gets in the way
statement: At most one tooltip MUST show at a time; a click or a page moving focus on load MUST NOT open one; Escape, leaving the control or moving focus away MUST close it.
group_name: Keyboard

title: Below 900 px wide the app has a compact top bar and fits the screen
statement: Below 900 px wide the app MUST take its phone layout. Its top bar MUST hold the menu button, the page's title on one line (cut with an ellipsis) under a link one step up (to the record's parent, a domain's product, or all products, keeping the view in front), and a quick find button. The layout MUST fill the screen's dynamic height (`100dvh`), keep its bars and sheets clear of the safe areas (`env(safe-area-inset-*)`, with `viewport-fit=cover`), and no page MUST scroll sideways at 320 px wide.
group_name: Phone

title: A phone keeps the stage filling the screen, switched from the page bar
statement: On a phone a record, group, product or domain page MUST show its stage filling the screen under the top bar and a compact page bar, with no resize handles: in the desktop app the Open pages button, then the stage switch (Graph, ERD and Trace, one pressed) and the wiki card button. Switching the stage MUST name it in the address (`?stage=erd`) and keep it in the place. The wiki card MUST open as a bottom sheet, on demand (`LA-V61-R20`).
group_name: Phone

title: The nav is a full-screen sheet with the same rows, sized for a thumb
statement: On a phone the nav MUST open from the top bar's menu button as a full-screen sheet that slides in from the left, keeps the space rail, takes focus to its quick find, keeps Tab inside it, and closes by Escape, its close button or choosing a page, giving focus back to the menu button. Its rows MUST be the wide screen's rows (`LA-V90-R03`), at least 44 px tall on a touch screen, with the fold chevrons as large targets.
group_name: Phone

title: The wiki card is a bottom sheet on a phone
statement: On a phone the wiki card MUST open as a bottom sheet over the stage, at half height, with a dimmed backdrop: it takes focus as it opens, keeps Tab inside it, and closes on Escape, a tap on the backdrop, a swipe down or its own close button, giving focus back to the control that opened it. A drag on its handle MUST take it to full height and back, settling by distance and speed.
group_name: Phone

title: In the desktop app, the open pages are a sheet
statement: On a phone-sized window of the desktop app the tabs MUST fold into an Open pages button in the page bar that shows how many are open and opens them as a bottom sheet: one row per tab with its ID and title, the active one marked, and a close button on every row. Choosing a row MUST go to that tab and close the sheet. The web app has no tabs of its own, so no Open pages button (`LA-V96-R32`).
group_name: Phone

title: Quick find opens at the top on a phone
statement: On a phone quick find, and the command palette it turns into after a ">", MUST open from the top bar (and from their shortcuts) as a full-width sheet at the top of the screen over the dimmed stage: the search box at the top with a Close button, the results as a list under it, each title wrapping rather than cut. Choosing a result MUST go there and close the sheet; Escape, Close or a tap on the stage MUST close it and give focus back. The shortcuts sheet MUST fill the screen.
group_name: Phone

title: The graph and the ERD pan, pinch and take taps
statement: The graph and the ERD MUST pan with a finger and zoom with a pinch. On a touch screen a first tap on a node MUST select it: the node is outlined and a card at the bottom of the canvas shows its kind and name; a second tap on it, or a tap anywhere on the card, MUST open it; a tap on the empty canvas MUST let it go. A click with a mouse MUST still open a node at once. A long press does nothing of its own: the tap's card is the preview.
group_name: Phone

title: Pages are readable on a phone
statement: On a phone body text MUST be at least 16 px, and every text box MUST be 16 px so the phone does not zoom in on focus. Long IDs MUST wrap rather than widen the page; wide tables and code blocks MUST scroll sideways inside their own box; long lists on a page MUST keep their ten rows with a search (`LA-TRC-SP02`), the nav's lists excepted (`LA-V90-R17`). A record row MUST stack: its ID on a line of its own, its title under it at the row's full width, and its meta (counts, tags, marks) below, so a title is never squeezed beside an ID.
group_name: Phone

title: The browser chrome follows the theme, and sheets move only when motion is welcome
statement: The page MUST carry a `theme-color` meta that follows the theme's sheet color, in light and dark and for any theme chosen. Sheets MUST slide in with the shared motion tokens and MUST appear at once when the system asks for reduced motion (`LA-PAT-APP-UX-R04`).
group_name: Phone

title: A tablet in landscape keeps the workbench, sized for touch
statement: The screen's width MUST decide the layout and the pointer the size of targets: at 900 px and wider, a tablet MUST keep the floating panels over the stage (nav, tab panel, wiki card), with every target at least 44 × 44 px on a touch screen (`LA-PAT-APP-UX-R07`); below 900 px, a tablet in portrait MUST take the phone layout.
group_name: Phone

title: The first load shifts nothing
statement: When a product, domain or record page first loads, nothing already drawn MAY move: content that arrives late (the specs, the fonts) MUST take room kept for it or appear without pushing what is drawn. The nav draws its lists once the specs have arrived; the fonts are the app's own, preloaded, and a font that is not there in time is not swapped in later.
group_name: Nothing jumps

title: Moving between records keeps the frame still
statement: Moving to another record through the nav, a link, a click on the stage, Back or quick find MUST keep the nav, the tab panel and the wiki card where they were, and MUST draw the new page at its place from its first frame: the wiki card's new page at the top, and a page reached by Back or Forward where it was scrolled. The nav's rows, the stage switch and the tabs' close buttons MUST NOT move: the stage switch holds the same three buttons on every page, and every tab has one width.
group_name: Nothing jumps

title: Collapsing or resizing a panel moves only it, and recenters the stage
statement: Showing, collapsing or resizing the nav or the wiki card MUST change only that panel: the other panels stay, the stage is not drawn anew, and the stage frames its focus again in the new open space with a short camera move on the shared motion (at once under reduced motion).
group_name: Nothing jumps

title: Folding moves only what is below the row
statement: Opening or closing a row, and Expand all or Collapse all, MUST move only what is below the row or the list; the row itself, the lists above it and the page title stay, and nothing jumps and then corrects.
group_name: Nothing jumps

title: Resizing follows the pointer
statement: Dragging a gap MUST resize what sits beside it with the pointer and never jump back to a size it left; folding a panel by drag moves nothing on the far side of the page.
group_name: Nothing jumps

title: The graph and the ERD stage keep their canvas still
statement: Re-centering the graph at any depth, changing the depth, and moving between a domain's, an aggregate's and an entity's ERD MUST keep the header strip, the stage's tools and the canvas at one size and place; only the boxes and the camera move, on the shared motion.
group_name: Nothing jumps

title: A live reload keeps what is in view
statement: When the specs reload while the Reader is scrolled part-way down, what was at the top of the view MUST stay there, and the graph MUST NOT be drawn anew.
group_name: Nothing jumps

title: Overlays are placed before they show
statement: A tooltip, quick find, the command palette and the shortcuts sheet MUST be placed before they show and stay where they showed; typing in their search box filters the list under it without moving the box.
group_name: Nothing jumps

title: Switching between color-only themes moves nothing
statement: Switching between themes that differ only in their colors (such as Lathe and Midnight) MUST change colors only: no box moves or changes size. A theme that sets its own typefaces, text size or panel radius (Graphite, Workshop, High contrast) MAY reflow text, and so resize what holds it.
group_name: Nothing jumps

title: The mobile sheets move nothing behind them
statement: At phone width (375 px), opening and closing the nav and wiki card sheets MUST NOT move the page behind them.
group_name: Nothing jumps

title: A page opens on the wiki's code alone
statement: A product, domain or record page MUST open on the wiki's own code: the Graph, ERD and Trace stages and the Appearance popover and theme editor MUST load with `import()` when first shown, so the first load reaches no ELK. The app's performance budgets are `LA-PAT-APP-UX-R11`'s.
group_name: Nothing jumps

title: The frame of a page holds still
statement: The nav, the tab panel, the wiki card and the stage MUST keep their place and size unless the Reader moves or resizes them; a change of page changes what they show, not where they are. Content that arrives after the page is drawn (the specs, the fonts, what the stage tells the header strip) MUST take room kept for it, arrive before paint, or be drawn where it pushes nothing the Reader can see.
group_name: Nothing jumps

title: A bar keeps one height, and a scroll box its gutter
statement: A bar that must not move (the header strip, every stage's toolbar) MUST have a fixed block size, or be one line cut with an ellipsis whose whole text is its tooltip, and text that changes in it MUST be one text, so a new number never moves what follows. A box that scrolls up and down MUST keep room for its scrollbar (`scrollbar-gutter: stable`), so its content keeps its width when the scrollbar comes and goes.
group_name: Nothing jumps

title: Every control is reached and worked by the keyboard
statement: Tab and Shift+Tab MUST reach every control a page draws, each with a visible focus ring, and go all the way round the page and back without being held anywhere. Inside a group of controls (the tab strip, a tree's rows) the arrow keys move and Enter or Space acts; in the graph, Tab moves between the boxes; elsewhere the arrow keys walk the stage by its keys (Left out and Right in in the Tree view, Up out and Down in in the Nested view; `LA-V93-R19`, `LA-V61-R49`). The main tasks MUST work by keyboard alone: open a record from the nav or from quick find, switch views, re-center the graph, fold and unfold a row, collapse and show the wiki card, and pick a theme.
group_name: Keyboard and screen reader

title: Focus lands where the Reader expects
statement: After a move to another page, focus MUST stay on the page, never fall to the body. A control that changes the page in place (a stage switch, a panel toggle, a fold button) MUST keep focus, and a panel collapsed from inside it MUST give focus to its toggle. Re-centering the graph by keyboard MUST put focus on the box that became the center. A dialog (quick find, the palette, the shortcuts sheet, the theme picker), a phone sheet (the wiki card, quick find, and in the desktop app the open pages) or a drawer (the nav) MUST take focus when it opens, keep Tab inside it while it is open, and give focus back to the control that opened it when it closes.
group_name: Keyboard and screen reader

title: What changes out of sight is announced
statement: When a command changes the page somewhere other than where focus is (a stage switched, the wiki card shown or collapsed, a theme chosen, every row folded), the app's one announcer (a polite live region) MUST say so in a short sentence, such as "Graph stage", "Wiki card collapsed" or "Color theme: Midnight".
group_name: Keyboard and screen reader

title: A control's name holds its visible text
statement: A control's accessible name MUST contain the text it shows, so a person who says what they see, or hears the name read, finds the same control. Where a control shows a count or a mark, the name is built from what is shown, with words for a screen reader added beside it in hidden text (`sr-only`), rather than an `aria-label` that says something else: the nav's Checks row is named "Checks 3 errors 12 warnings", and a space's button, which shows a monogram the reader is not meant to hear, is named by its product's title in hidden text, with the mark hidden. An `aria-label` that stays MUST include the shown text as a word: "Open pages: 2".
group_name: Keyboard and screen reader

title: No control inside another
statement: A control MUST NOT hold another control: a screen reader reads the outer one as one thing and cannot reach the inner one. Where two act on one item, they sit side by side in a plain wrapper, as a page tab and its close button do.
group_name: Keyboard and screen reader

title: A box that scrolls can be reached by keyboard
statement: A box that scrolls on its own and holds nothing that takes focus (a code block, a stage's key bar, the shortcuts sheet's groups) MUST take focus itself (`tabindex="0"`) and be named as a region, so the arrow keys can scroll it.
group_name: Keyboard and screen reader

title: A target is at least 24 px, or has room around it
statement: On any pointer, a link or control that is not inside a sentence MUST be at least 24 by 24 px, or stand far enough from its neighbors that a 24 px circle on it touches no other target (WCAG 2.2, 2.5.8). Record links listed in a table cell or the wiki card are drawn one line tall at 24 px. On a coarse pointer the larger 44 px of `LA-PAT-APP-UX-R07` applies.
group_name: Keyboard and screen reader

title: Text sits only on the surfaces the theme vouches for
statement: Body text and muted text MUST be drawn only on the surfaces whose contrast every built-in theme guarantees: the page (`--paper`) and a sheet (`--sheet`), which the theme contrast audit holds to 4.5:1 in light and dark. The shell (`--shell`) is the gap between panels and holds no text: a page that is one panel, such as Checks or Appearance, draws its own `--paper` background rather than let the shell show through.
group_name: Keyboard and screen reader

title: Arrow, WASD and HJKL keys walk every stage's levels, except in arrow controls
statement: On a record, group, product or domain page, the stage walk MUST move over the stage shown (Graph, ERD or Trace) from anywhere on the page, without the stage having keyboard focus first: the plain arrow keys, with the plain letters W, A, S and D, and vim's H, J, K and L, doing exactly what Up, Left, Down and Right do (W and K Up, A and H Left, S and J Down, D and L Right), and Shift+Up (or Shift+W or Shift+K) going out to the container and Shift+Down (or Shift+S or Shift+J) in to the first node inside it, the same on every stage, the Graph included, as the stage toolbar's buttons do (`LA-PAT-APP-UX-R21`); all through the same walk and the same guard, each move moving the stage's focus as a click does. Each stage MUST be walked as a hierarchy: the Graph its tree; the ERD the product, each domain's region, each aggregate's area and each entity; the Trace its five columns, each box in its column. An arrow MUST move among the siblings, the nodes of one level in the same container: on the Graph by the layout's keys (`LA-V93-R19`); on the Trace Up and Down within a column and Left and Right along the links to the nearest linked box (`LA-V98-R09`); on the ERD by where the boxes sit on the map, never by the record tree. At a container's edge an arrow MUST go on to the next container's first node at that level in reading order (left to right, top to bottom) going Right or Down, or to the previous container's last going Left or Up, so repeated presses visit every node at a level; from the product an arrow goes in, Right and Down to its first node and Left and Up to its last. On the ERD an arrow MUST go to the nearest sibling that way by the boxes' centers: those overlapping the current box's row (Left and Right) or column (Up and Down) first, then the shortest distance. Faded boxes count: a step into a faded area brings it into focus. A focus that picks out no box walks from its domain's region. On the Trace stage, on a gap's box the walk MUST move the keyboard's ring, announced, and leave the focus where it is. One handler in the commands layer MUST do it for every stage. A plain arrow, one of those letters, or Shift with Up, Down, W, S, K or J, MUST stay with the element that has keyboard focus when that element uses arrows itself (so a letter is always typed where text is taken): a text field, a textarea, a select, editable text (the chat's message box), a radio group, a slider, a focusable splitter (a panel's resize handle), a menu or menu button, a listbox or combobox (quick find, the command palette, the theme picker), a tab list, a modal dialog, a box that took focus to scroll by them (`LA-V61-R46`), and an element marked as handling arrows itself (a tree list's rows, the chat log, the breadcrumb's menu, and the Trace table under its canvas). The nav's links do not use arrows: with one focused, as after a click in the nav, the arrows walk the stage. Arrows and letters with Cmd, Ctrl or Alt MUST keep their own meanings, and Shift with Left, Right, A or D does nothing new. Clicked into, the wiki card MUST NOT scroll by the arrows; Page Up, Page Down, Space and the pointer still scroll them. When a step leaves keyboard focus where it was (anywhere but a graph box, from which focus follows to the new focus's box and is read out there), the new focus MUST be announced in the page's live region by its kind and title.
group_name: Keyboard and screen reader

title: Every page has its own address
statement: Every page MUST have its own address that can be bookmarked, shared and reloaded, and the browser's back and forward buttons MUST move between pages.

title: A key another shortcut has is offered as a swap
statement: When the key recorded belongs to another shortcut where both apply, the sheet MUST say so at once, naming that shortcut, and offer Swap (this shortcut takes the key, the other gets the key given up) or Cancel (nothing changes). Any other refusal (a key the browser keeps, a shortcut left without a key) MUST show its reason in the row, the last key's removal offering to leave the shortcut without a key.
group_name: Keyboard

title: Recording a key works from the keyboard and a screen reader
statement: The recording control MUST take focus and be named for what it does ("Press a key for <shortcut>. Escape cancels."); a modifier alone waits for the key; Escape cancels without closing the sheet, and Tab or leaving it cancels too, so focus is never trapped; the key pressed MUST reach no command. The result MUST be announced, and focus MUST go back to the row (or to Swap when a swap is offered).
group_name: Keyboard

title: Editing works from the keyboard and a screen reader
statement: Every aggregate's record actions, its forms and its remove question MUST work from the keyboard alone, as the rest of the app does: every input labeled, a required input marked as required, an input with a problem marked invalid and described by its message, focus taken to the form's first input when it opens and back to its action when it closes, and a change announced. They MUST pass the accessibility suite (`LA-PAT-APP-UX-R10`) with no finding.

title: A page reads again only what a change touched
statement: When the server sends `spec:changed` naming read models, an open page MUST read again only the reads of those read models, keeping every other answer it has; one naming every read model, or none, MUST read everything again. After the page's own write it MUST wait for the server's change for that write and read again only what it names, reading everything again only when no change comes within 300 ms or no channel is open.

title: Appearance lists the themes, each previewed live on the stage
statement: Appearance MUST open as a popover over the stage from its button at the foot of the nav, and from the command palette ("Open Appearance settings"), at `?panel=appearance` on the current focus. It MUST offer light, dark or system, and list every theme, built in and the Reader's own, each with a chip of its colors, the one in use marked: pointing at or focusing a theme MUST preview it live on the whole app, the stage included, and clicking it MUST keep it. Each theme MUST have a button to duplicate and edit it (built in) or edit it (the Reader's own), and to export it.

title: A copy of a theme can be edited, renamed, reset and deleted
statement: "Duplicate and edit" MUST make a copy and open it in the theme editor, a larger panel over the stage (`?panel=theme&theme=<id>`), with: color pickers grouped by purpose (surfaces, text, borders, accent, signals, graph and depth), the light and dark sets side by side; fonts for headings, text and code from a short safe list or a custom font stack; text size, density (comfortable or compact), panel corner radius, gap between panels, and motion (follow the system or always reduced). The theme being edited MUST be the one in use, so the app around the editor is its live preview, beside small light and dark previews. The editor MUST rename the theme, reset it to the built-in it was copied from, and delete it after asking, going back to Appearance.

title: Hard-to-read colors are flagged while editing
statement: While editing, each text or control color whose contrast on what it is drawn on falls below WCAG AA (4.5:1 for text, 3:1 for large text and controls) MUST show a warning beside its swatch, with the ratio, the background and the ratio it needs, for the mode it fails in.

title: Themes are kept per person and travel as files
statement: The reader's own themes, the chosen theme and the mode MUST be kept per person (in the browser's local storage, behind a store the desktop app can replace), and MUST survive a reload. Any theme MUST export as a small, versioned file, and such a file MUST import as a new theme of his own.

title: Appearance turns Scroll to zoom on or off
statement: Appearance MUST have a Scroll to zoom switch, off by default, that sets what scroll does on every stage (`LA-V93-R07`): off, scroll pans and Cmd or Ctrl with scroll zooms; on, scroll zooms and Cmd or Ctrl with scroll pans; a line under it MUST say which, as it is now. The command palette MUST have the same as a command ("Turn scroll to zoom on or off"), which announces the new state. Either MUST apply at once, in every tab and on every stage, and MUST be kept per person from one launch to the next (`LA-PLT-A4-SR01`).

title: The Color theme command previews each theme and keeps or puts back
statement: The "Color theme" command (`chooseTheme`, g then t) MUST open a quick pick of every theme. Arrowing to a theme MUST show it on the whole app at once, without keeping it; Enter or a click MUST keep it, and Escape or a click outside MUST put back the theme shown before.

title: Light, dark or system is chosen in the app
statement: Every theme MUST show its light or dark set by the person's choice of System (the default, following `prefers-color-scheme`), Light or Dark. The choice MUST be made by the "Light, dark or system" command (`chooseColorMode`), which previews like the theme picker, and on Appearance.

title: Quick find and the command palette are one overlay; the shortcuts sheet is searchable
statement: Cmd/Ctrl+P (or Cmd/Ctrl+K) MUST open one search box in the upper middle of the window over a lightly dimmed stage, on records; a query that starts with ">" (or opening it with Cmd/Ctrl+Shift+P) MUST list every command that applies on the current page instead, filtered as the Reader types, and deleting the ">" MUST go back to records. A command MUST apply only while what it acts on is shown: a stage hidden while the next one loads MUST stop answering its commands at once, and answer again once shown. Up and Down MUST move through the results, Enter MUST go to the record or run the command, and Escape or a click on the dimmed stage MUST close it. The nav's "Go to…" button with its shortcut hint, the rail's Quick find button, the phone's top bar and the desktop command center MUST open it. The shortcuts sheet MUST list every shortcut grouped as Navigate, View, Graph and Lists, with a search box. Both MUST be dialogs that take focus, keep Tab inside, close with Escape and give focus back.

title: Menus and quick find's commands show each command's keys at the right
statement: Quick find's commands, and any menu, MUST show each command's first shortcut right-aligned on its row in `<kbd>` styling; a command without one shows none.

title: Quick find jumps to anything by ID or title
statement: Quick find MUST find any record, domain or product by ID or title, best matches first (exact ID, ID prefix, title), and MUST let the Reader move through the results with the arrow keys and open one with Enter. Each record result MUST show its kind chip, its ID and its title, and a short trail of the places above it in the one breadcrumb's collapsed form (`LA-PAT-APP-UX-R16`), so similar titles can be told apart.

title: Quick find searches the current space only
statement: Quick find MUST search only the current space's records (and the record format's kinds and checks), as one list for the arrow keys, and MUST NOT list anything of another product: switching product is the rail's job.

title: Quick find finds kinds and checks
statement: Quick find MUST list every kind as "Kind: <label>" and every check as "Check: <name>", found by their names and labels, each leading to its page.

title: A highlighted record previews on the stage
statement: While a record result is highlighted and the highlight rests, the stage MUST glide to it and the wiki card MUST show it in its compact summary, without moving the address, the tabs, the header strip or the card's own More or Less setting. Enter MUST commit (the address moves there); Escape or any other close MUST return the camera, the wiki card (with its scroll and setting) and keyboard focus to where they were. Under reduced motion the stage MUST move at once, with no glide. A command, or a page of the record format, MUST NOT preview.

title: Quick open is an accessible dialog
statement: Quick open MUST be a modal dialog named for its mode (Quick find, or Command palette) holding a combobox that controls a listbox and names the highlighted option with `aria-activedescendant`; keyboard focus MUST stay in the box while the arrows move the highlight, and MUST return to where it was when it closes. Its text and chips MUST pass AA contrast in every look. Arrow keys pressed in its box MUST move its highlight only, never the stage.

title: The shortcuts sheet matches the hints
statement: The shortcuts sheet (`?`) MUST list the same keys the hints show, with one "Switch to <product>" row per product that has a key.

title: The record format is a command and a link in the shortcuts sheet
statement: The record format MUST NOT be a link in the nav's footer or rail. It MUST be the "Record format" command in the command palette (g then f) and a link in the shortcuts sheet; the desktop app's Help menu has an entry too. The footer MUST keep saying where the data comes from.

title: The menus are File, Edit, View, Window and Help
statement: The shell MUST have native menus: File (Open Product Folder…, Open Recent, Close Window), Edit, View (the app commands, then Reload, Force Reload, Toggle Developer Tools, the zoom items and Toggle Full Screen), Window, and Help (Record Format, Keyboard Shortcuts), with the app menu first on a Mac.

title: A menu choice runs the app command by its ID
statement: A menu item for an app command MUST send the command's ID from the keymap (such as `stageGraph` or `toggleNav`) to the page, and the app's command system MUST run it, as if its key had been pressed.

title: The menus show the person's keys without taking them
statement: An app command item MUST show the key the keymap names for the menu (the command's menu key) as its window's page last sent it (LA-PLT-CMD59), or the first key the person bound to it instead, when a menu can show it (a chord with Cmd, Ctrl or Alt, or a function key); and MUST NOT take the key: off a Mac the accelerator is not registered, and on a Mac the page gets each key first. The menu lists no key of its own. Only Settings and the keys a browser keeps for its tabs and history are the menu's own.

title: Open Recent lists the last 10 folders
statement: File › Open Recent MUST list the recent folders, latest first, each opening its folder, then Clear Menu; with none it MUST say No Recent Folders.

title: Settings opens the app's settings in the focused window
statement: Settings… (Cmd+,) MUST open Appearance over the stage (`?panel=appearance`) in the focused product window.

title: The window has no system title bar; the app draws its own
statement: A window MUST have no system title bar.
