The app MUST draw its own 38 px bar across the top of the window, on the shell color (`--shell`) with no border, so the bar and the shell are one surface, and lay the page out under it. On macOS the traffic lights MUST float over the bar's left end, centered in its height; on Windows and Linux the native window controls MUST draw over its right end. The bar MUST leave room for them. The window MUST keep its title and, on macOS, its represented folder, which the Window menu and Mission Control show.

title: Back and forward follow the app's history
statement: The bar MUST start with back and forward buttons that run the app's `goBack` and `goForward` commands. Each MUST be disabled when there is no page to go to in that direction, where the browser can tell.

title: The command center names the page and opens quick find
statement: The bar's center MUST hold a command center: a pill showing the product name and the current page's heading ("Lathe — Add an item to the basket"), centered on the window and cut short with an ellipsis when it does not fit. Clicking it MUST open quick find (`quickOpen`), and its tooltip MUST show the shortcut.

title: The layout toggle shows and hides the navigation
statement: The bar MUST end with a toggle button for the navigation that runs `toggleNav`, the same command as the menus and the keys. It MUST say with `aria-pressed` whether the nav shows, and its tooltip MUST show the shortcut; while the nav is collapsed for space (`LA-PAT-APP-UX-R18`), its tooltip and name MUST say so.

title: The bar drags the window, and a double-click zooms it
statement: Dragging the bar anywhere but on a control MUST move the window. Double-clicking it there MUST zoom or maximize the window, as the system's setting says. Its controls MUST take clicks and never drag.

title: The window's chrome follows the theme
statement: When the theme or the light or dark mode changes, including the system's appearance while the mode is System, the app MUST send the theme's shell and ink colors to the shell through `window.latheDesktop.setChrome`. The shell MUST then set the window's background and, on Windows and Linux, the window controls' colors.

title: In a browser there is no title bar
statement: The app MUST draw the title bar only when `window.latheDesktop` is present. In a browser the page MUST stay as it is.

title: A window opens on the shell color with a launch view until the specs answer
statement: A new window MUST show the theme's shell color at once and a launch view (the logo and "Opening <product>…") until the page has the product's specs, with no white flash and no blank window.

title: A folder the engine cannot load gets an error page with a way on
statement: When Lathe cannot start for a folder or the engine cannot load it, the window MUST show the message with Retry, Open Another Folder and Reveal in Finder.

title: A launch, error or About page runs only the buttons it shows
statement: A button press from the shell's own pages MUST run only when it is one of the actions that page shows, and only from that page.

title: About Lathe shows the versions and links to the repo and the record format
statement: About Lathe MUST open a small window with the app's, the engine's and Electron's versions and links to the repo and the record format, opened in the system browser. Check for Updates MUST NOT show until signed builds are published.

title: The app icon reads at every size and in light and dark Docks
statement: The app MUST have an icon drawn on Apple's icon grid, rendered from SVG for macOS (`.icns`, 16 to 1024 px), Windows (`.ico`) and Linux (PNGs), with a bolder drawing at 16 and 32 px. A development build (`npm run dev`) MUST show the icon with a "DEV" band in the Dock.

title: The Dock menu opens a new window and lists recent folders
statement: The Dock menu MUST have New Window, which runs Open Product Folder, and every folder opened MUST be added to the system's recent documents, which macOS lists in the Dock menu.

title: The Dock badge follows the window in front
statement: The badge MUST show the number of check errors of the focused product window's current space, its product's and the workspace's as its Checks panel counts them, or of the window focused last while another app is in front; it MUST follow that window when the data reloads or the space changes, and show nothing when there are none. A count MUST be a whole number from 0 up, from the window's own page; anything else MUST be ignored.

title: The graph is a stage of a page, not a place in the nav
statement: The graph MUST be reached as the stage of the page in hand (its button in the stage switch, Ctrl+G or Alt+G, Ctrl+1, the command palette), never as a separate item in the side navigation.

title: A group that is a record links; a group the app computes only folds
statement: A group that is a record (a capability, a use case, an aggregate) MUST link to its page wherever it heads its members; a stage or kind group MUST NOT pose as a record: its nav row only folds and its heading is not a link.

title: A selected row is the whole row
statement: In the nav, as in VS Code's explorer, a row MUST be as wide as the nav panel, indented by padding for its depth rather than by nested margins, with its indent guides and its fold chevron inside it. The current page's row MUST carry the selection over the whole row, from the panel's left edge over the indent and the chevron to its right edge, in the selection tint with its text and chevron in steel, with no bar of its own at its edge. A hovered row MUST take the hover tint over the whole row, and while the nav is used from the keyboard the selected and the focused row MUST show a 1 px steel outline. The lists stay nested for screen readers.

title: The menu lists each product and its domains
statement: The left menu MUST show each product as a space in its rail, and list the current space's domains (with their capabilities) in its panel.

title: The nav collapses to a rail, and is a full-screen sheet on a narrow screen
statement: A toggle MUST collapse the nav to a narrow rail of icons (the logo, Quick find, the spaces, Checks), each with a tooltip and an accessible name, and expand it again; the state MUST be remembered. When the window can't hold every open panel even with the wiki card collapsed, the nav MUST collapse to its rail for space, last (`LA-PAT-APP-UX-R18`), leaving the remembered state alone. Under about 900 px wide the nav MUST become a full-screen sheet opened from the menu button in the top bar, with focus moved into it and kept inside it, and closed by Escape, its close button or choosing a page, with focus returned to the menu button.
group_name: Read a record several ways at once

title: The nav folds by section and shows where you are
statement: The Tools section, and each domain and folder of the current space, MUST each fold and unfold with a chevron button carrying `aria-expanded`; the section holding the current page MUST open itself. The current space MUST have no heading of its own, since the rail names it: its first row is its overview. The current page MUST be marked clearly with `aria-current="page"` and scrolled into view. Icons MUST be inline line icons; counts MUST be quiet badges, with errors red and warnings amber on Checks; long names MUST be cut short with the full name as a tooltip; items MUST be at least 32 px high. A footer MUST say where the specs come from (the record format is a command and a link in the shortcuts sheet, as `LA-V65-R71` says).
group_name: Read a record several ways at once

title: The rail lists each product as a space
statement: The nav MUST have a rail about 56 px wide at its far left with one square icon per product in the products' ID order, and no item above every product. Each item MUST name itself in a tooltip.
group_name: Work in one product at a time

title: The current space is marked
statement: The rail MUST mark the current space with an accent bar and `aria-current`.
group_name: Work in one product at a time

title: The nav lists only the current space's things
statement: The nav MUST list the current space's product page, its domains, each folding into its five stages as the schema places kinds (with the capabilities in order under Use cases), and its groups (the product's other kinds of children), and MUST NOT list another product's domains.
group_name: Work in one product at a time

title: Choosing a space opens the last page visited in it
statement: Choosing a space MUST open the last page visited in that space during the session, or its product page when there is none.
group_name: Work in one product at a time

title: Alt and a number switch spaces
statement: Alt+1 to Alt+9 (⌥1 to ⌥9 on a Mac) MUST switch to the first nine spaces in rail order, and the command palette MUST offer a "Switch to <product>" command for each, with its keys. Every other shortcut MUST keep working.
group_name: Work in one product at a time

title: The rail stays in the nav sheet on a narrow screen
statement: On a narrow screen the rail MUST stay visible inside the nav sheet.
group_name: Work in one product at a time

title: No view in a space shows another product
statement: Inside a space the header strip, the wiki card (its History included), the graph and its minimap, the ERD and Trace stages, hover cards, the reference's records and its "where the X are" links, saved tabs and the space's last page MUST show only that product, and the desktop Dock badge MUST count only its problems and the workspace's. A link into another product MUST NOT be drawn or listed, and another product's ID named in a text field MUST show as plain text, not as a link.
group_name: Work in one product at a time

title: The nav reads like stage folders
statement: Under the current space, the nav MUST list the product page; then Shared, only when it holds anything, holding the patterns, the standards and the records with no owner that two or more domains use, or none (one that a single domain uses sits in that domain, `LA-EXP-DS03`); then each domain, which unfolds into its five stages, then its open questions.
group_name: Read a product laid out in stage folders

title: Stages and folders fold one level at a time, with counts
statement: Every domain, stage and folder MUST be a foldable row showing one level when opened; only the level under the space MUST show by default. A stage with one folder MUST list that folder's records itself, with no folder row (`LA-PAT-APP-UX-R15`). Each stage and folder MUST show its count of records, and one with no records MUST NOT be listed. An opened folder MUST list all its records plainly, inline, in the nav's one scroll: no filter box, no count line and no scroll box of its own (quick find finds a record among many).
group_name: Read a product laid out in stage folders

title: The current page's branch opens itself
statement: Opening a page from the nav, or on the nav's first draw (a load, a reload, the nav expanded or opened as a drawer), MUST open the nav rows that hold it: a domain page its domain; a record page its domain and stage (or Shared), its folder when the stage has more than one, and the parents above it in that stage; a group page the folder of its kind. A page opened anywhere else (a link in the page, the graph, Back, quick find) MUST leave the nav's rows where they are (`LA-V61-R28`): the closed row that holds the page is marked instead, and opening that row opens the branch down to the page.
group_name: Read a product laid out in stage folders

title: Use cases lists capabilities, then use cases outside any
statement: A domain's Use cases stage, which holds only capabilities and so lists them itself (`LA-PAT-APP-UX-R15`), MUST list the domain's capabilities in their order, then the use cases outside any capability; a capability's own use cases stay under it. A use case's flows MUST be listed in Interaction design and a requirement's tests in Test plan.
group_name: Read a product laid out in stage folders

title: Technical and test kind folders fold in the nav, with counts
statement: In the side nav, Technical specification's and Test plan's kind folders MUST be foldable rows with their counts, one level shown by default, and the current page's branch MUST open itself through its stage and kind folder. A kind folder's row MUST only fold. What is folded MUST last for the session.
group_name: Read the technical specification and test plan by kind

title: Records with no owner sit in the domain that uses them, or in Shared
statement: Records with no owner (value objects and their constraints, views and their requirements, integrations, UI components) MUST be listed in the one domain that uses them, or else in their product's Shared, by stage, and a specification in its domain's Domain model, in the nav and on the domain and product pages alike.
group_name: Read the technical specification and test plan by kind

title: The rail shows only with two or more products
statement: The space rail MUST show only when the workspace shows two or more products. With one, the nav MUST show no rail and its panel MUST take the rail's width, its first row the product's name and icon; collapsed, the nav MUST keep its buttons and list no spaces.

title: A space's last page lasts the session
statement: The last page visited in each space MUST be remembered for the browser session only, never across sessions.

title: What is folded in the nav lasts the session
statement: Which nav rows are open MUST be remembered for the session only, never across sessions.

title: Standards sit in the technical specification stage of the nav
statement: The nav MUST list a product's standards in the technical specification stage, beside its patterns under Shared.

title: A domain has one page, at its ID
statement: A product's and a domain's only page MUST be their overview, at their bare ID (`/LA`, `/LA-EXP`); there MUST NOT be a second, generic record page for them. That one page MUST lose nothing the generic page showed: in the wiki card its text, kind, fields, data file, parent, children, links out and in, and problems.

title: The domain page groups records by stage
statement: The domain page MUST group its records by its five stages, each record under its parent where the parent is of the same stage (an aggregate's invariants, a use case's requirements).
group_name: Find a record in a domain

title: A search box filters records by ID or title
statement: The domain page MUST have a search box that filters the shown records by ID or title as the reader types.
group_name: Find a record in a domain

title: The domain page shows its coverage gaps and problems
statement: The domain page MUST list the domain's coverage gaps (each with the missing link) and the problems about its records.
group_name: Find a record in a domain

title: The domain page and group pages use the same folders as headings
statement: The domain page MUST head its records with the same stages and folders as the nav (the five stages), listing a folder's records directly or under one heading per kind when it holds several, a stage with one folder listing its records under the stage's own heading with no folder heading (`LA-PAT-APP-UX-R15`), and keeping its one-level-deep folding. A group page MUST name the stage and folder of its kind, such as Interaction design.

title: Technical specification lists records by technical kind
statement: A domain's Technical specification MUST list its records by technical kind, in the plan's order (repositories, data models, tables, value types, predicates, event types, projections, command handlers, query handlers, event handlers, services, UI components, endpoint handlers, adapters, then the product's own kinds), each record with what it names in code: its file, or a table's name.
group_name: Read the technical specification and test plan by kind

title: Test plan lists tests by test kind
statement: A domain's Test plan MUST list its tests by test kind in the plan's order (constraint, invariant, specification, policy, domain service, use case, view, endpoint, flow, integration, pattern rule and standard rule tests), each with its run by: its level, its file when automated, and its state.
group_name: Read the technical specification and test plan by kind

title: The domain page and group pages head the same groups
statement: The domain page MUST head Technical specification's and Test plan's kind groups with the same names and order as the nav, keeping its one-level-deep folding of records and its filter. A group page of tests MUST read them in the same groups.
group_name: Read the technical specification and test plan by kind

title: Endpoints and integrations sit in Interaction design
statement: The nav, the domain page and the graph MUST place an endpoint in its domain's Interaction design, and an integration in the Interaction design of the one domain whose flow steps exchange with it, or else of its product's Shared, by its kind's stage in the meta-model.

title: The domain page's coverage shows every obligation kind and the tests by state
statement: The domain page's Coverage section MUST show one group of bars per obligation kind the engine reports, the pattern rule line among them, each with designed, built, proved and not-automated-yet counts, then the domain's tests by state. Its gaps MUST name each obligation, pattern rules included, that the domain does not yet design, build or prove.
group_name: Traceability

title: View and API requirements are listed under their view or endpoint
statement: The domain page MUST list each view requirement and API requirement nested under its view or endpoint, and each record of an obligation kind a product adds under its parent, with its gaps and problems on its row. Searching for one MUST keep its view or endpoint shown above it.
group_name: Traceability

title: Each test shows its state, and one not automated yet never looks like proof
statement: The domain page MUST tag each test with its state. A test not automated yet MUST look unfinished and MUST NOT be counted or drawn as proof.
group_name: Traceability

title: A domain page lists the patterns it follows
statement: A domain page MUST have a Patterns we follow section listing each pattern that the domain itself follows ("followed by the whole domain") or that any of its use cases follows, with the use cases that follow it. Each pattern's rules MUST be folded under its row, one level deep like the rest of the page, and each rule, owed by the domain (LA-TRC-SP04), MUST show whether this domain proves it (the tests coverage counts as its proof there), both as the engine's coverage says and never worked out by the page itself, with a test not automated yet shown apart. A domain that follows no pattern MUST say so.
group_name: Traceability

title: A page writes only through its aggregate's commands
statement: A page MUST change a record only when the person acts on one of its record actions, and then only by sending one of its aggregate's own commands, `POST /api/<aggregate>/<command>`, which that aggregate's handler applies or refuses whole. Until then a page MUST only read, each through its own query (`GET /api/<aggregate>/<query>`, and the stages' and the Record page pattern's reads: the meta model, the record summaries, the folder tree, the problems, coverage, the record trace and the record changes). Opening, reading or searching a page MUST NOT send a command, and no page MUST write a data file itself, so every change is one the aggregate's rules accept and is reviewed in git.

title: A list of one kind is titled by that kind, through plural()
statement: A list of a record's children or a group's members MUST be titled by its kind's plural label, through `plural()`, when it holds one kind ("Invariants", "UC requirements", "Components"), and MUST be titled "Children" or "Members" only when it holds more than one kind to tell apart. Its count stays beside the title, and its accessible name and search box follow the title ("Invariants of LA-EXP-A1", "Filter domain rules"). A group's label MUST read as plain English, and any kind it names MUST come from the workspace's kind labels through `plural()`, such as "Command handlers", so a product that renames a kind sees its own name.

title: Grouped requirements and rules read under their group headings
statement: The wiki MUST show a record's children that name a group, such as a use case's requirements, a view's view requirements, an endpoint's API requirements, a pattern's rules or a standard's rules, under their group headings: the ungrouped ones first, without a heading, then each group in the order it first appears. A use case's requirement table and a standard's rule table MUST head each group's rows with its name.
group_name: Read a record several ways at once

title: A test's page shows its state
statement: The record page MUST show a test's state; for a test not automated yet it MUST look unfinished and say that it does not count as proof.
group_name: Traceability

title: An obligation lists what designs, builds and proves it
statement: An obligation's record page MUST show a Traceability section after its text and before its children, with these groups in this order, each left out when empty: Designed by, Built by (Met by, for a standard rule; each marked built or not built) and Proved by (each test with its state), holding exactly what the obligation's chain holds as the engine works it out, the chain the Trace stage draws, then its other incoming links under their reverse labels, then its links out under their forward labels, leaving out the records its chain already shows. The app MUST NOT work out a chain of its own. A group is titled by its links' label and holds each record once.
group_name: Traceability

title: Each gap shows as a callout linked to its check
statement: An obligation's Traceability MUST name each gap in a callout, "Not designed yet", "Not built yet" or "Not proved yet", saying when its test is not automated yet, taken from coverage's own gaps for the domain that owes it, never from a count of its own, so it never disagrees with the coverage marks or the checks. Each callout MUST link to the page of the check that reports it (`not-designed`, `not-built`, `not-proved`). A pattern rule MUST show one line for each domain that owes it, judged from that domain's test alone.
group_name: Traceability

title: A technical record and a test show what they implement, prove and run from
statement: A technical record's Traceability MUST show what it implements, then that record's tests, rolled up, then its other links under their labels. A test's MUST show what it proves (its parent), then its run by: its level, its state, and the file that runs it, flagged when the file is missing, or its manual reason. Any other kind MUST show its links out under their forward labels and its links in under their reverse labels.
group_name: Traceability

title: A desktop record page offers its data file actions and a native menu
statement: In the desktop app a record page's facts MUST offer Reveal in Finder, Open in editor and Copy ID for the data file that holds its row, and a right-click on its title, a record link or a graph node MUST ask for the native record menu, while a right-click elsewhere keeps the page's own. In a browser the page MUST show none of them.

title: A test's run by shows its size and markers
statement: A test's run by MUST show its size (small when it gives none) and its markers, and a test MUST show the test data sets it starts from.
group_name: Traceability

title: A test's or record's page lists the outcomes it measures
statement: A test's or record's page MUST list the business outcomes it measures, under Measures.
group_name: Traceability

title: Every kind opens its aggregate's own page
statement: Every one of Lathe's kinds MUST open its aggregate's own page (`PAGES`, total over Lathe's kinds), and a kind a product declares the Extension record page; the Record page shell MUST NOT draw a record by reading its columns.

title: Every record's page names the outcomes it serves
statement: Every record's page except a business outcome's and the product's MUST show among its facts a Serves line read through get-serves: each outcome it serves as a link, or, when none reaches it, that no use case reaches it, with a link to the serves-no-outcome check for an aggregate, read model or obligation.
group_name: Traceability

title: Motion carries no meaning and stops under reduced motion
statement: Motion in the graph MUST only help the eye follow a change: the view after a move MUST be the same with or without it, and when the system asks for reduced motion the camera MUST jump to the new view with no glide.

title: By touch, a tap selects a node and a second tap opens it
statement: A finger has no hover, so on a canvas a first tap on a node MUST select it and say what it is before anything moves, and only a second tap on the same node, or a tap on the card that names it, MUST open it. A pointer that can hover opens a node with one click.

title: A canvas stays mounted and is fitted before it paints
statement: The graph and the ERD stage MUST keep their canvas mounted while their content changes, MUST fit their first picture before it paints, and MUST NOT cut a glide short by fitting again when neither their size nor the open space has changed.

title: Domain events are flags
statement: Wherever a domain event is drawn as a node or box in the graph, it MUST be a flag, notched on the right (`LA-V93-R06`), in its stage's colors as every record is (`LA-V93-R12`), so events read the same in every layout.

title: A domain is drawn as a hexagon
statement: In the graph every domain node MUST be drawn as a hexagon, with flat top and bottom edges and pointed left and right ends, drawn as a polygon, not a rotated box. The points' chamfer MUST grow with the node's box scale (12 map units at box scale 1), at most a quarter of its width, so a very tall domain still reads as a hexagon and not as a diamond. Its border MUST follow the outline in every state, hovered, focused, keyboard-focused and selected by a tap, by coloring and thickening the outline's own edge, drawn inside the polygon. A parent line into a domain MUST meet the tip of its point, and a parent line out of one MUST start on its slanted side, where the outline is at the child's middle; a line meets every other shape's outline the same way (`LA-V93-R06`). The minimap draws boxes.

title: Each kind is drawn in a shape of its own
statement:
In the graph every kind MUST have one shape, the same in every view, as a secondary cue after its label, and every shape MUST keep a rectangular footprint so boxes still stack:

| Group | Kind | Shape |
|---|---|---|
| Structure | product | a large rounded box |
| | domain | a hexagon (`LA-V93-R05`) |
| | stage, folder and group | a folder with a tab |
| Domain model | aggregate | a double border |
| | entity | a plain box |
| | value object | a plain box with a tag mark |
| | constraint, invariant, specification | an octagon |
| | policy | an octagon with a gear mark |
| | domain event | a flag, notched on the right |
| | command | a slanted box |
| | query | a slanted box with a lens mark |
| | read model | a plain box with a lens mark |
| | domain service | a plain box with a gear mark |
| | term | a plain box with a marker mark |
| Use cases | capability | a slice pointing right |
| | use case | a stadium |
| | UC requirement | a page with a folded corner |
| | pattern | stacked boxes |
| | pattern rule | an octagon |
| Interaction design | flow | a chevron bar |
| | flow step | a chevron |
| | view | a window with a top bar |
| | view requirement, API requirement | a page with a folded corner |
| | endpoint | a box with a port notch on its left |
| | integration | a plain box with a port mark |
| Technical specification | table | a striped box |
| | repository, data model, value type, rule, predicate, event type, projection, command, query and event handlers, service, UI component, endpoint handler, adapter | a box with component tabs |
| | standard, standard rule | stacked boxes and an octagon, with a ruler mark |
| Test plan | every test kind | a shield |
| Other | open question | a diamond |

A kind a product adds MUST be a plain box. In the Tree view a box's outline MUST be its kind's shape: a polygon shape drawn with its edge inside the polygon, so its border, hover, focus, keyboard ring and a tap's selection color and thicken the outline itself, and a rounded shape with its border's corners and its rings following them. In the Nested view every box MUST keep its rectangle and show its kind's shape as a small mark before its kind and ID line. A shape's corners and notches MUST grow with its box's scale, at most a share of its side. Its label and problem badge MUST stay inside its shape's safe area, which the map keeps when it wraps and sizes the label, so no line is clipped or crowded by a notch or a corner. Every shape and mark MUST be in the graph's key (`LA-PAT-APP-CODE-R21`).

title: The map is drawn on a canvas, anew each frame
statement:
Focusing a node, by a click, the address, Back and Forward or the step keys, MUST move the camera only: it MUST frame the focus and the levels the depth shows below it to fill the open space the floating panels leave over the stage, with the parent's level kept in view in a strip at the left edge. That opening frame MUST take whole rows of the focus's level, its edges in the gaps between them, and end on the right in the gap before the next column. What lies outside the focus's subtree is drawn faded by the focus fade (`LA-V93-R73`). The camera's zoom limits MUST let it frame the deepest leaf of a large product, which is very small against the product's box (`LA-EXP-DS06`), and fit the whole map on a phone: at most as far in as draws the map's smallest box 400 pixels on its shorter side, and never less than 256 times the map's units, so the limit grows with the map; a ten-thousandth at least. The framed levels MUST fit the open space; the depth decides only what is framed; the focused box is always whole in it (`LA-PAT-APP-UX-R23`). The camera MUST move there from the view as it is, including one the person zoomed or panned, in one smooth zoom and pan (zooming out only as far as the pan needs) on the shared motion (`--motion-speed`, `--motion-ease`, at most twice the speed for a long path); on a page's first picture, on a resize of the stage and under reduced motion it MUST go there at once. Free zoom and pan move the same camera, by one wheel rule on every stage (the Graph, the ERD and the Trace) that the person's Scroll to zoom sets (Appearance, `LA-PLT-A4`). With Scroll to zoom off, the default and Figma's convention, scroll (a mouse wheel or a two-finger trackpad swipe) MUST pan by the screen pixels it scrolled, down and across at once on a trackpad; Shift with scroll MUST pan sideways, a wheel's vertical scroll turned horizontal unless the browser already turned it; and Cmd or Ctrl with scroll MUST zoom about the pointer. With Scroll to zoom on, scroll MUST zoom about the pointer; Cmd or Ctrl with scroll MUST pan, down and across at once as a trackpad scrolls; and Shift with scroll MUST pan sideways, as with it off. Either way a trackpad pinch MUST zoom about the pointer (the browser sends a pinch as a scroll with Ctrl set, so it is told from Ctrl with scroll by whether the Control key is down), every zoom within the zoom limits and a line or page of scroll scaled to pixels; a scroll MUST keep the move it began with, pan or zoom, its momentum included, and a key pressed or let go during it that changes that move (Cmd or Ctrl, or Shift with Scroll to zoom on) MUST stop it, the rest of that scroll dropped until it pauses or a new scroll begins; a drag pans; panning never changes the zoom or the focus; and the zoom buttons zoom about the open space's middle; a gesture during a glide takes over from it, and the frame button and the `.` command frame the focus again.

The map MUST be drawn on a canvas, anew for each frame of the camera. A viewport MUST be kept in doubles, and every map point placed on screen in doubles relative to the camera's center, with no transform but the screen's pixel ratio, so a box deep in a large map is as steady at a deep zoom as at the top. Each label's lines MUST be drawn at their size in the map times the zoom, so text is crisp at any zoom whatever the map's range. A visually hidden layer of the drawn boxes, in the keyboard's order, MUST carry focus, Tab, the arrow keys, Enter and Escape, and each box's role and name for assistive technology, and the box it focuses is drawn with the focus ring. The pointer MUST find the box under it from the map's own outlines (a box's rectangle, a shape's polygon or rounded corners), the last drawn first, so a child drawn over its parent is found before it.

title: Depth frames levels of the nav's tree below the focus
statement: The Graph stage of `/<record-id>` (`?stage=graph`, the default stage) MUST show the one map of the nav's tree, stages and folders included (see LA-EXP-DS04, LA-EXP-DS05), and at depth N (1 by default, up to 3) MUST frame the record, its parent at the left edge and its descendants down to N levels below it (see LA-EXP-DS09), with no cross-links: at depth 1 its parent (or folder) and its children (or their folders). The graph MUST draw no link between records other than the parent lines: a record's other links are the Trace stage's (`LA-V98`) and the wiki card's. `/graph` on its own MUST open the first product.
group_name: Walk the model as a graph

title: Clicking a node re-centers the graph and changes the address
statement: Clicking a record node MUST re-center the graph on that record and change the address to its page, so Back walks back along the path, and MUST keep how the graph is drawn, in the tab it is made in (LA-V93-R72). The header strip's breadcrumb MUST name where the new focus sits in the tree (`LA-PAT-APP-UX-R16`).
group_name: Walk the model as a graph

title: Node and line style show kind, stage, errors and gaps
statement: Nodes MUST be colored by their stage, each of the six stages its own color, structure nodes their own and shaped by kind (see LA-V93-R06), a domain drawn as a hexagon (see LA-V93-R05), parent lines MUST be drawn solid in ink, and records with errors or coverage gaps MUST carry a visible mark. The stage's key bar (LA-V96-R30) MUST explain each style the graph draws around its focus, and the change marks while there are any: a new record's pill, outline and tint, a changed record's, a removed record's dashed ghost, and the dimming of everything unchanged while Highlight changes is on (LA-V96-R29).
group_name: Walk the model as a graph

title: Kinds can be switched off
statement: The reader MUST be able to hide and show each kind. The graph draws only the tree, so it has no relation filters.
group_name: Walk the model as a graph

title: The graph works from the keyboard
statement: Tab and Shift+Tab MUST move between the drawn nodes, Enter MUST focus the record or group with keyboard focus, and Escape MUST clear the filters. Keyboard focus MUST always be visible.
group_name: Walk the model as a graph

title: The graph is one map in columns that follow the parent/child tree
statement: The graph MUST be laid out left to right in columns by depth in the parent/child tree, one map for the product's tree (see LA-EXP-DS05): the product furthest left, then each level in its own column; the focus's ancestors to its left and its descendants to its right. Every record with the same parent, record or group, MUST sit in the same column whatever its kind (see LA-EXP-DS05). Parent/child lines MUST be drawn as the solid spine of the tree, passing through a group in its own column where the parent's children are grouped (see LA-EXP-UC04). Links MUST NOT move anything: every record keeps its place in the map.
group_name: Walk the model as a graph

title: Focusing moves the camera, not the map
statement: When the person focuses a record or group, the map MUST hold still: no node moves or changes size, and the camera glides, in one smooth zoom and pan on the shared motion, to frame the new focus and the levels the depth shows below it (see LA-EXP-DS09). The first picture of a page appears at once. When the system asks for reduced motion, nothing MUST animate: the camera jumps to frame the focus (see LA-V93-R01). Every canvas stage works this way (`LA-PAT-APP-UX-R19`). New data MUST move only what it changed (`LA-PAT-APP-UX-R22`): what a new layout moves glides from its old place to its new one, and the camera stays where it is, gliding with the focus only when the focus's own box moved.
group_name: Walk the model as a graph

title: Hovering a node spotlights it and what it joins
statement: Hovering or keyboard-focusing a node MUST brighten it, its lines and the nodes it joins directly, and dim the rest a step; leaving MUST restore the picture. It MUST change with the motion tokens, and at once under reduced motion.
group_name: Walk the model as a graph

title: Arrows step out, in and across by the view's keys, Shift+Up out, Shift+Down in
statement: The plain arrow keys MUST step through the tree from anywhere on the page but a control that uses arrows itself (`LA-V61-R49`), each step moving the graph's focus. In the Tree view, which draws parents beside their children, Left MUST step to the parent, Right to the first child, and Up and Down to the previous and next sibling in the nav's order. In the Nested view, which draws children inside their parent, Up MUST step to the parent, Down to the first child, and Left and Right to the previous and next sibling in the nav's order. In every view Shift+Up MUST step to the parent and Shift+Down to the first child. The sibling steps MUST never loop: past the last sibling the next step goes on to the first child of the next parent at that level in the tree's order, and before the first the previous step to the last child of the previous parent at that level (`LA-V61-R49`), so repeated steps visit the whole level; where no parent at that level follows or precedes, it does nothing. Stepping out of the root or in to a node with no children MUST do nothing. From a box, keyboard focus follows. A step MUST keep how the graph is drawn, its layout and depth included, and stay in its tab (LA-V93-R72). The arrow keys MUST never step with Cmd, Ctrl or Alt held, nor with Shift beside Left and Right. The moves MUST be listed in the shortcuts sheet with their keys, and the stage toolbar's step buttons (`LA-PAT-APP-UX-R21`) MUST keep their order in every view, each showing its arrow and letter and named, in its tooltip too, by the step it takes in the view shown, with `aria-keyshortcuts` naming its keys; no other shortcut with a modifier steps.
group_name: Walk the model as a graph

title: A minimap shows the whole map and where the view sits
statement: A Minimap switch under Filters, off by default and kept for the session, shared by every tab, MUST show a minimap in a corner: a true overview of the one map, its upper levels as boxes (as many as stay readable), the focus solid and the camera's view outlined as it moves, colored through the theme's tokens.
group_name: Walk the model as a graph

title: A Tree, Nested or Map switch
statement: The graph's toolbar MUST offer a Layout switch of Tree, Nested and Map, Tree by default, kept with the session's graph settings, which moving through the graph never changes (LA-V93-R72), never in the address, with a command and its shortcut (`v`, which steps to the next layout: Tree, Nested, Map, then Tree again) in the command list. Tree draws the one map as an icicle, each parent beside its children (`LA-EXP-DS05`). Nested draws the same tree as boxes inside boxes: the product made of its domains, a domain of Define and Design, a stage of its folders, a folder of its records (`LA-EXP-DS07`), explored by the same camera (`LA-EXP-DS09`). Map draws the product as ground, its domains as districts, every record one size and its links as lines (`LA-EXP-DS12`, `LA-V93-R74`). Depth 1 to 3 frames the Tree view; the Nested camera frames the focus's box and the Map's frames it at street level, so they have none, and there the Depth buttons are neither shown nor reachable, though they keep their place (`LA-EXP-DS09`). Everything else the graph does MUST work the same in all three: a click, Enter or a tap to focus, the hover spotlight, the arrow keys stepping through the tree, Tab through the drawn boxes with a visible focus ring, `.` to frame the focus again, Filters (a hidden kind keeps its space), the fit and zoom buttons, the minimap, Back and Forward with the camera's glide, the problem and coverage marks, and the same roles and accessible names.
group_name: Walk the model as a graph

title: Folders and records with several kinds of children are reached through one group each
statement: The graph MUST draw the nav's stages and folders as group nodes (a stage with one folder holding that folder's records itself, with no folder node, `LA-PAT-APP-UX-R15`), and when a record's children, or a folder's records, include more than one kind the nav lists side by side, MUST put a group node per kind between them, labeled with the kind's plural label and the number of members, such as "Use cases (5)". A group MUST be drawn like a folder, differently from records. The parent/child spine MUST run record, group, record. Every group is a level for the depth. Hiding a kind hides its kind groups (a stage or named folder has no kind of its own).
group_name: Walk the graph through folder-like groups

title: A group shows its name and count, and clicking it goes to its address
statement: A group MUST show its name and count. Every member is always in the map, so there is nothing to open or fold in place, and a group has no chevron or other control of its own. Clicking the group, or pressing Enter on it, MUST go to its address, as clicking a record does.
group_name: Walk the graph through folder-like groups

title: A group has its own address and can be the center
statement: A group MUST be the focus at its own address: a stage or folder at `/<domain-id>/<stage>[/<kind>]`, for example `/TL-LEND/domain-model/aggregate`, and a kind group at `/<parent-id>/<kind>`; the folder of a stage with only one has no address (`LA-PAT-APP-UX-R15`). At depth 1 the camera MUST frame its parent at the left edge and all its members to the right, and depth counts levels from it as from a record. Its wiki page names the parent and lists every member. The focused record's wiki page MUST link to its groups. The breadcrumb trail and the browser's Back button MUST work for groups as for records. An address for a group that does not exist MUST say so.
group_name: Walk the graph through folder-like groups

title: A group carries a mark when anything inside it has problems or gaps
statement: A group MUST carry the error, warning and coverage-gap marks that records carry whenever any member, or any record beneath a member, has them, so a group whose members are too small to draw still shows where the trouble is. The graph's key MUST explain groups and their marks.
group_name: Walk the graph through folder-like groups

title: Groups take their own column between a parent and its children
statement: A group MUST sit in its own column, one after its parent's and one before its members', so the graph still reads left to right. In the map each parent's children are a column of their own (`LA-EXP-DS05`), so a group sits one depth level after its parent, as the records at the same depth under other parents do.
group_name: Walk the graph through folder-like groups

title: Domain events sit under their aggregate
statement: In the graph, an aggregate's domain events MUST sit under it through a "Domain events" group, by the one-kind rule, and each event MUST be drawn as a flag (`LA-V93-R04`). The `raises` links into an event and the `hears` links of the policies that hear it are not drawn in the graph; the Trace stage and the wiki card show them, labeled from the meta-model ("Raised by", "Heard by").
group_name: Walk the graph through folder-like groups

title: A parent is as tall as its children, so the tree reads like an icicle
statement: In the map, a record, stage, folder or group MUST be as tall as its children stacked, each an equal part of it, and each child MUST sit right beside it, joined by a short, level parent line, so the tree reads like an icicle and no lines fan out from a parent to its children (see LA-EXP-DS05). A parent's children MUST share one width, a share of their parent's that narrows the more children share it (LA-EXP-DS05), and siblings MUST share one text size, in proportion to their width or as large as every sibling's whole label allows, centered, the title wrapped on whole words (see LA-EXP-DS06). No node's size ever depends on what is in focus.
group_name: Walk the graph through folder-like groups

title: The graph shows pattern rules under their pattern
statement: In the graph a pattern's rules MUST sit one column to its right, under it. A domain's or use case's `follows` link is not drawn in the graph; the Trace stage and the wiki card show it.
group_name: Walk the graph through folder-like groups

title: In the graph a flow step sits under its flow
statement: In the graph a flow step MUST sit one column to the right of its flow, joined to it by the parent line, and, as for other children, MUST reach them through a group only when the flow also has children of another kind.
group_name: Walk the graph through folder-like groups

title: The graph reaches components and tests through the same groups
statement: In the graph a domain MUST reach its technical records and its tests through their stage and kind groups, as the nav does, and each record keeps its own place in the map (DS05)
group_name: Walk the graph through folder-like groups

title: The graph draws standards with a ruler
statement: The graph MUST draw a standard and its rules in the technical specification stage's color, shaped as a pattern and a pattern rule with a ruler mark (`LA-V93-R06`), and its key MUST say so.

title: Moving through the graph never changes how it is drawn
statement: How the graph is drawn MUST never change by moving: its layout and minimap, one reader setting for the browser session shared by every tab, and its depth and kind filters, the place's own (LA-V96-R14); none is part of the address. The arrow steps, a click or Enter on a box, a link, a tab switch, and Back or Forward MUST keep them, in the tab moved in and in a new tab, which copies the depth and filters. Only the person changing a setting MUST change it: the toolbar's switches and filters, and the `v`, `+` and `-` keys. A reload MUST bring them back.
group_name: Walk the model as a graph

title: The focus and what lies under it are drawn at full strength, the rest faded
statement: In every layout (Tree and Nested) the graph MUST draw the focus and everything under it at full strength, and everything else (its siblings, other branches and the levels above it) faded well back, at the focus fade (`--focus-fade`, about a quarter of its strength). In the Nested layout each ancestor that contains the focus MUST keep a faint outline and name as a trail (`--focus-trail`), while its other contents fade. A line MUST be drawn as faint as the fainter of the boxes it joins. The fade MUST follow the focus, however it moves (the arrow keys, a click, Enter, the address, Back and Forward), and ease with the camera's glide to it, at once under reduced motion. A faded box MUST still answer the pointer: hovering it spotlights it at full strength (`LA-V93-R17`), and a click makes it the focus. The focus's subtree keeps its full contrast; the faded context is decoration.
group_name: Walk the model as a graph

title: The Map shows domains as districts, every record one size, its links as lines
statement: In the Map layout (`LA-EXP-DS12`) the graph MUST draw the product as ground, each domain and the shared records as a district (a soft labeled area, not a box), a stage as a neighborhood in its stage's tint and a folder as a lighter area, each named with its count of records at one size on screen; records stand on the areas, every leaf one size, a record holding only its composition (`LA-STD-MODELING-R14`). The focus's links, and the links of a box a first tap selects, MUST draw as lines over the boxes, each from the side facing the other end, named by its relation by the focus where they meet (one name for each relation there), its parent drawn as a link (In capability) where the map does not hold it; no other link is drawn unless All links, a switch under Filters shown only in the Map, off by default and kept with the session's graph settings, draws every link between the records drawn (at most 400). Nothing fades: the focus is ringed. Zoomed out, records become blocks, then only the areas' names and counts read, districts last; the change roll-ups and problem marks stay on the containers. The walk, quick open and Frame land at street level (zoom 1), the focus whole and centered: a record, district, neighborhood or area too big to show whole there is zoomed out until it fits (`LA-PAT-APP-UX-R23`). The arrows walk the Map's own tree, Up out and Down in, Left and Right across (`LA-V93-R19`); a kind group of the Tree's, which the Map does not draw, frames its nearest box above. The toolbar MUST offer Tidy up in the Map (the stage's shared button and command, `t` by default), which packs the Map afresh in reading order; new data otherwise keeps every box where it was (`LA-EXP-DS12`). The key MUST name District, Part of and Link.
group_name: Walk the model as a graph

title: Each domain is a region of the map
statement: The ERD map MUST draw each of the product's domains as a region labeled with its name, holding its aggregates, in the domain model stage's colors, and a reference to another domain's aggregate MUST run between the regions. Each region MUST be laid out to about the map's 1.6:1 shape: its aggregates' layers wrapped into rows or its unconnected parts packed side by side, whichever comes nearer, so a large domain never stands taller than wide. Zoomed out until a region's head is too small to read, each region's name MUST show over its head at a readable size.

title: Each aggregate is a boundary around its entities
statement: The ERD map MUST draw each aggregate as a boundary containing its entities, the root marked, each entity with its fields: each field's name and type (a basic type, a value object's name, or "→ Aggregate" for a reference). It MUST draw a has one or has many line between entities, with crow's-foot ends, and a dashed reference-by-ID line from an entity holding a field typed by another aggregate to that aggregate's root (see LA-EXP-DS11). A domain with no aggregates, and an aggregate with no entities, MUST be a closed box that says so. The ERD stage MUST draw nothing but domains, aggregates, entities and these lines: no command, domain event, policy, specification, read model or query.
group_name: Read a domain and its aggregates as an ERD

title: An aggregate's focus keeps it whole and fades the rest
statement: On an aggregate the ERD stage MUST draw its boundary, its entities, their fields and their has one and has many lines at full strength, and every other box and line faded back (see LA-PAT-APP-UX-R19), its domain's region and the reference lines to the aggregates it references or that reference it among them; the camera MUST frame its boundary.
group_name: Read a domain and its aggregates as an ERD

title: An entity's focus picks it out in its aggregate
statement: On an entity the ERD stage MUST keep its aggregate at full strength, pick the entity out and frame it, never zoomed in past 1, so the boxes around it show.
group_name: Read a domain and its aggregates as an ERD

title: Boxes lead to their pages, and the key lists what the map draws
statement: Clicking a box, or pressing Enter on it, MUST go to its page, keeping the stage, and a box MUST show a hover state; the box of the record in focus leads nowhere. The stage's key bar (`LA-V96-R30`) MUST list only what the map draws, from: domain, aggregate boundary, entity, root entity, has one, has many and reference by ID, with the picked-out box and the faded boxes when there are any, and MUST explain the change marks while there are any: a new record's pill, outline and tint, a changed record's, a removed record's dashed ghost, and the dimming of everything unchanged while Highlight changes is on (LA-V96-R29).
group_name: Read a domain and its aggregates as an ERD

title: Outside the focus's scope boxes fade, and the frame fits what it frames
statement: Boxes and lines outside the focus's scope MUST be faded with the graph's focus fade (see LA-EXP-DS09), easing with the camera's glide, out of focus and out of the keyboard order. The frame MUST fit what it frames inside a margin and the open space at any window size, never zoomed in past 1, and edge hints MUST count the boxes in focus past each edge.
group_name: Read a domain and its aggregates as an ERD

title: Any other record frames its nearest entity or aggregate, or its domain or product
statement: On a record that is not a domain, an aggregate or an entity the ERD stage MUST keep its domain at full strength and pick out and frame its nearest entity or aggregate above it in the tree (a table its entity), or its domain's region when it has none; on a Shared record (one in no domain) or a product it MUST frame the whole map, nothing faded. A product with nothing to draw MUST say so in words.

title: The ERD is one map laid out once: focusing moves the camera
statement: The ERD stage MUST be one map of the whole product (LA-PAT-APP-UX-R19), laid out in ELK's worker, and again only when what the layout reads changes (a box, its title, its fields or a line), never on a reload that left it alone. Focusing a record, by a click, the keyboard, the arrow keys or the address, MUST NOT move any box or change its size: only what fades (the shared fade), what is picked out and the camera change, the camera gliding with the shared camera and framing on the shared framing, or jumping under reduced motion. A stage switch MUST keep the focus and show the map already framed on it, and tell the wiki card where the picked-out box sits. The map MUST be drawn on the shared canvas, each frame only what is on screen, and below the zoom at which a box's title would be drawn under 5 pixels every box MUST be drawn as a plain block, with no title or fields (`LA-EXP-DS10`); its boxes, with their fields, MUST be in a visually hidden layer for the keyboard and assistive technology, a map of more than 150 boxes keeping there only the boxes in view.
group_name: Read a domain and its aggregates as an ERD

title: Tidy up lays the whole map out afresh
statement: New data MUST keep every ERD box where it was (`LA-PAT-APP-UX-R22`): a region and the product's top level keep their boxes' places, a box that grew pushes only what it overlaps, right or down, a new box goes beside the rest, and a removed one leaves its room. The stage's toolbar MUST offer Tidy up, also a keymap command (`t` by default, rebindable like every command), that lays the whole map out afresh in ELK's worker, its order worked out again to shorten its lines; the boxes and their lines glide to their new places on the shared motion (at once under reduced motion), the camera following the focus's box. Every later change keeps its places from the tidied layout.
group_name: Read a domain and its aggregates as an ERD

title: Every page opens the graph on its Graph stage, not from the nav
statement: Every record, group, product and domain page MUST open its graph on its own Graph stage (the stage switch in the page bar, Ctrl+G or Alt+G, Ctrl+1 and the command palette), the stage a page shows by default. The side navigation MUST NOT have a Graph item, open or as a rail: the graph is a stage of a page, not a place of its own.

title: The graph is a component that any page can host
statement: The graph MUST be a component that takes its focus (a record ID, or a parent ID and kind) and reports every move to a new center through a callback, without reading or changing the address itself, so the focus page can show it as its stage. It MUST fill the stage and frame the focus in the open space it is given, and frame it again when the stage's size or the open space changes.

title: A record or group has one address, whatever the stage
statement: A record MUST be shown at its bare ID (`/<id>`), a product and a domain included, and a group of the graph's tree at its place in it: a stage at `/<domain-id>/<stage>` and its folder at `/<domain-id>/<stage>/<kind>` (none for a stage with one folder, `LA-PAT-APP-UX-R15`), a record's kind group at `/<parent-id>/<kind>`, in every view.
group_name: Read a record several ways at once

title: Graph, ERD and Trace are stages switched in the page bar, named in the address
statement: A record, group, product or domain page MUST show one stage at a time, full window behind every panel: Graph, ERD or Trace. The stage switch MUST sit with the page's controls (`page-bar-actions`): at the right of the page bar in the desktop app and on a phone, and at the right of the header strip's row on the web; a group labeled "Stage" of `aria-pressed` icon buttons in that order, one pressed; every stage MUST be offered on every page (`LA-PAT-APP-UX-R17`), so no button is ever disabled, dimmed or hidden. The buttons MUST have a visible focus ring and their shortcut in their tooltip, and switching MUST keep keyboard focus on the button. The stage MUST be written to the address as `?stage=` and its name, such as `?stage=erd`, so a shared link opens as it was seen; an address with no stage MUST show the graph. The stage last chosen MUST be remembered for a space's first place. There MUST be no panes, no side-by-side views, no pane gaps and no full screen mode.
group_name: Read a record several ways at once

title: The stage frames the focus in the open space the floating panels leave
statement: The stage MUST measure the floating panels' own rectangles (never widths assumed in code) and frame its focus in the open space they leave, less its own floating tools: the graph's camera and the ERD's fit center the focus there, and the Trace stage pads its content into it and scrolls under the panels so the chain or the focused row sits in it. The stage toolbar MUST sit inside the open space, clear of every panel, the nav's rail included, also after the page changes between the phone and the wide layout. Collapsing, opening or resizing any panel MUST recenter the focus with a short camera move on the shared motion, at once under reduced motion. The Graph and ERD stages MUST pan freely under the panels. A stage's own toolbar at its top MUST have the open space's whole width at its row as its room (right of the nav, left of the chat; the wiki card sits below the row), and MUST sit centered on the whole stage, whatever panels are open or collapsed, while it fits there; when it is wider than that it MUST stay inside its room, against the nav or the chat, rather than fold its walk away (LA-PAT-APP-UX-R21).
group_name: Read a record several ways at once

title: The stage, header strip and wiki card follow one focus, moved together by Back
statement: Clicking a record on the stage MUST change the address, so the header strip and the wiki card follow; following a link in the wiki card MUST focus that node on the stage. Back and Forward MUST move them all. The graph's depth, filters and open groups MUST survive moving between pages and switching stages.
group_name: Read a record several ways at once

title: A group has a simple wiki page
statement: A group's wiki page MUST show its parent (as a link), its kind (with the kind's description), and its members as a list, each with its coverage marks and problem badge.
group_name: Read a record several ways at once

title: Product and domain pages have the same stages
statement: A product's and a domain's overview pages MUST offer the same three stages as any page, with their overview in the wiki card: the graph centered on the product or the domain, the domain's or the product's ERD, and the trace of their obligations.
group_name: Read a record several ways at once

title: The header strip names the focus in one line under the page bar
statement: Directly under the page bar, the header strip MUST name the focus in one line about 28 px high, whatever the stage: its breadcrumb up the tree (`LA-PAT-APP-UX-R16`), then its kind, ID and title, and at the right what the stage draws of it (such as "9 records · 8 links"). On the web, wide, where there is no page bar (`LA-V96-R32`), it MUST be the tab panel's one row instead, as high as a page bar, with the page's controls (`page-bar-actions`) at its right after the counts, so no row stands empty. The title MUST be cut with an ellipsis, its whole text in its tooltip and read in full by assistive technology; the strip is the page's h1. No stage MAY keep a header of its own above it.
group_name: Read a record several ways at once

title: Moving never leaves the tab
statement: In the desktop app every move (a click on a box or a link, the arrow and WASD walk, Out and In, quick find, the wiki card's links, Back and Forward) MUST change only the place of the tab it is made in and MUST NOT activate another tab, even one that holds the record moved to. A record MAY be open in several tabs, each its own place.
group_name: Explore several places at once in tabs

title: A new tab opens only on request, after the active one
statement: In the desktop app a new tab MUST open only when the Reader asks: Cmd or Ctrl+click or a middle-click on a box or a link, Open in New Tab in a record's right-click menu, Cmd or Ctrl+Enter in quick find, Cmd or Ctrl+T (a new tab on the product), or Duplicate Tab. A new tab MUST copy the active tab's stage, depth and kind filters, focused on what was opened, with a fresh history; Duplicate Tab MUST copy the active tab with its history. It MUST open after the active tab and become active, except on a middle-click, which opens it in the background as a browser does.
group_name: Explore several places at once in tabs

title: A tab closes by its button, a middle-click, Cmd+W or Alt+Shift+W
statement: In the desktop app each tab MUST have a close button, shown on hover, on focus and on the active tab. Middle-clicking a tab MUST close it, and Cmd or Ctrl+W (the menu's Close Tab) and Alt+Shift+W (`closeTab`) MUST close the active tab; File › Close Window takes Cmd or Ctrl+Shift+W. Closing the active tab MUST activate its neighbor to the right, or else to the left, and move the address there; closing the last tab MUST leave one tab on the product.
group_name: Explore several places at once in tabs

title: Ctrl+Tab cycles the tabs, and the strip works as a tab list
statement: In the desktop app Ctrl+Tab (`nextTab`) and Ctrl+Shift+Tab (`previousTab`) MUST activate the next and previous tab in tab order, wrapping at the ends, and with the other tab commands (`newTab`, `closeTab`, `duplicateTab`, `openRecordInNewTab`, `goBack`, `goForward`) MUST be listed in the shortcuts sheet and the palette, their keys in tooltips and `aria-keyshortcuts`. Activating a tab, by a click or a key, MUST move the address to its place. The strip MUST be a `tablist` of `tab` elements with `aria-selected`, only the active tab in the Tab order; with a tab focused, the arrow keys, Home and End MUST move between tabs, Enter or Space MUST activate the focused one and Delete MUST close it.
group_name: Explore several places at once in tabs

title: Each tab keeps its own place
statement: Each tab MUST keep its own place: its focus, stage, camera, depth, kind filters, the wiki card's open and expanded state and scroll, and its history; activating it MUST bring them back as they were. The graph's layout, the minimap and the wiki card's width MUST NOT be a tab's: they are one setting for the session, which no move and no tab changes (LA-V93-R72).
group_name: Explore several places at once in tabs

title: Tabs are kept per space for the session and come back on reload
statement: In the desktop app the open tabs, their order, which one is active, and each tab's place with its history MUST be kept per space for the browser session; switching spaces MUST swap the tab set for that space's own. Reloading MUST bring back every tab, the same active tab, and each tab's place and history. A saved tab, history entry or space's last page that is not a page's address MUST be dropped.
group_name: Explore several places at once in tabs

title: The desktop app's tab strip leads the page bar, each tab with ID and title
statement: In the desktop app the tab strip MUST sit at the left of the page bar, at the top of the tab panel floating over the stage; on the web the page bar holds no tabs (LA-V96-R32). Each tab MUST show its record's ID in mono and its title, cut short with an ellipsis, with both in full in its tooltip, never in italics; a group's tab MUST show its label ("Use cases (7)"). Tabs that do not fit MUST scroll sideways by wheel or trackpad, and the active tab MUST scroll into view; the page bar keeps its height. On a phone-sized window the tabs MUST fold into an "Open pages" button in the page bar that opens them as a sheet (`LA-V61-R21`).
group_name: Explore several places at once in tabs

title: View › Tabs holds the tab commands in the desktop app
statement: View › Tabs MUST offer New Tab, Close Tab, Duplicate Tab, Show Next Tab, Show Previous Tab, Back and Forward, running `newTab`, `closeTab`, `duplicateTab`, `nextTab`, `previousTab`, `goBack` and `goForward` by command ID. The menu MUST own Cmd+T, Cmd+W, Ctrl+Tab, Ctrl+Shift+Tab, Cmd+[ and Cmd+] (Ctrl off a Mac) as their accelerators, since a web page never receives some of those keys, and File › Close Window MUST move to Cmd or Ctrl+Shift+W.
group_name: Explore several places at once in tabs

title: The ERD stage works on every page
statement: Every page MUST offer the ERD stage, switched like the Graph and sitting after it: the product's one map, framed on the page's domain, aggregate or entity, and on any other page on its nearest entity or aggregate, or its domain or product (LA-V94-R07, LA-V94-R08, LA-PAT-APP-UX-R17). An address that names it MUST show it on any page.

title: The wiki card shows the settled focus's wiki page, resizable and collapsible
statement: The wiki card MUST show the focus's wiki page, with its editing, floating at the right of the open space over whichever stage shows: from the open space outward, the wiki card, then (in the desktop app) the chat, the nav alone on the left; it is how a page is read, and there is no Wiki view. It MUST float in the map as a callout in one constant spot, never docked to the stage's edges and never following the focus up or down: its top just under the stage's own toolbar row (never level with it), a gap of 28 px at its right and the same above it and below it (well wider than the panels' own 8 px). Its height MUST be a steady share of the stage, never its content's: about 60% of the stage's height as a summary (`LA-V96-R22`) and about 85% expanded, always above the foot by its gap; longer content scrolls inside, and shorter content leaves room below it inside the card. It MUST read as part of the graph and stand clear of it: the boxes' kind line (the kind and the ID), the sheet's round corners (`--sheet-radius`, 14 px, clearly rounder than a box's 4 px), a 2 px border all round in the focused box's own color (its stage's edge color, as the graph draws its outline and the leader line), following the focus, so the box, the line and the card read as one object (the system's text color under forced colors) and a lifting shadow, its text keeping WCAG 2.2 AA contrast. It MUST follow the focus (a click, the arrow keys, Tab, a link, a tab, Back and Forward), drawing a new page at once after a rest and, while the focus moves again within a moment (arrowing through the stage), only once it settles, so it never draws a page per step; the new page MUST cross-fade in gently, with no fade under reduced motion, and MUST show whole without relying on the fade to finish: a page drawn while the window is hidden (where animations pause), or hidden mid-fade, ends its fade at once. A link inside it MUST focus that node on the stage. It MUST be resizable by its left edge (360 to 900 px, a third of the open space until set, and never narrower than 360 px) and collapsible by its button, the page bar's toggle and the keys: Enter MUST show it when collapsed and collapse it when open, wherever keyboard focus is but a control that handles Enter itself (a link, a button, a field, a menu, a list's options, the chat box, a dialog), a graph box included (Enter on another box focuses that box; on the focus's own box it toggles the card), with Ctrl+W (Alt+W off a Mac) for the same command; Escape MUST collapse it once nothing above it is open, each overlay (quick find, a menu, a dialog, a tooltip, a tool panel) closing first, and a field keeping its own Escape. Collapsed from inside the card, focus goes to the page bar's toggle; from the stage, it stays where it was; its open state and width MUST be the session's setting, never a tab's. When the window can't hold it at 360 px, it MUST collapse for space first, before the nav (`LA-PAT-APP-UX-R18`), its open state unchanged. On a phone it MUST be a bottom sheet, opened on demand.

title: Panels float over the stage, frosted, and opaque under reduced transparency
statement: The nav, the tab panel and the wiki card MUST float over the stage as inset, rounded panels with a soft shadow: a mostly opaque surface over a backdrop blur, so the stage shows through as shape and color while their text keeps WCAG 2.2 AA contrast, the dense panels (the nav, the tab panel and the chat, about 82%) nearer opaque than the wiki card (about 80%), over a blur (22 px) strong enough that the stage behind reads only as shape and color. Muted text MUST keep 4.5:1 against a panel composited over any fill the stage draws in a built-in theme and over dense content (about a quarter ink over the paper), and the wiki card's text at least 4.8:1. Their surfaces MUST be tokens with light and dark values, and under `prefers-reduced-transparency: reduce` every panel MUST be opaque.

title: The stage redraws only when its camera or its data changes
statement: The stage MUST draw again only when its camera moves or what it draws changes, never when a panel's content does (the wiki card drawing a page, the header strip's counts). A camera move with every panel open MUST stay within its budget in the performance suite (`LA-PAT-APP-UX-R11`).

title: The wiki card opens as a summary, and More shows the whole page in place
statement: The wiki card MUST open as a summary of the focus: the kind line (the kind and the ID), the title, the whole statement, goal, meaning or description, never cut short, and at most three key facts for its kind (its parent first, an obligation's coverage as designed, built and proved, then its own short fields, such as a use case's actor, and its children's count). A More button MUST expand it to the whole wiki page in place, and Less MUST take it back; whether it is expanded MUST be the place's, with its open state (LA-V96-R14), and its width the session's. Edit and Add MUST stay in reach in both. The card's height MUST NOT follow what it shows: about 60% of the stage as a summary and about 85% expanded (`LA-V96-R19`).

title: A leader line joins the focused box to the wiki card, on every stage
statement: Like a digital map's callout, a leader line MUST join the focused box on the stage to the wiki card that shows it, on every stage (the Graph, the ERD and the Trace), drawn one way for all of them: a thin line from the focused box's nearest edge to the card's inner edge, ending level with the card's title, with a small dot at each end, read from where the card actually is (so it slants when the two are not level). It MUST be drawn on the stage's own canvas, under the floating panels, in the focus's own color (the color of its outline), at a width that reads but stays fainter than a link. It MUST follow the camera every frame (a pan, a zoom, a glide, an arrow step) and the card's place and width (a resize, another panel collapsing), drawn in the same frame, never a frame behind. It MUST always be one straight segment, drawn over any box in its way rather than bent around it. When the focused box is off-screen or behind a panel, it MUST become a short stub at the open space's edge, pointing toward the box. It MUST NOT be drawn while the card is collapsed, on a phone (the card is a bottom sheet) or with no single focused box drawn; under forced colors or more contrast it MUST use the system's highlight color. It is decorative: hidden from assistive technology, since the card already names its record. It MUST add no measurable cost to a camera move (LA-V96-R21).

title: The wiki card's summary facts wrap at the card's width
statement: In the wiki card's summary, each key fact's label column MUST be as wide as its longest label and the value MUST take the rest of the card's width, so a long value (a flow's or a parent's title) wraps at the card's width, never in a narrow column beside its ID.

title: History in the wiki card lists the commits that changed the record
statement: The expanded wiki card (More) MUST end with a History section that reads git only when asked: a "Show the history" button, and once pressed the commits that changed the focused record's rows in the data files, newest first, each with its date, author, subject and short hash, twenty at a time with "Load more". Changes in the working tree not committed yet MUST come first, labeled "Not committed". Each commit MUST show what it changed in the record's rows, the fields before and after, marked with the theme's tokens. When the product folder is not a git repository, or git is missing, it MUST say so calmly, as a hint, not an error. A group has no rows of its own, and says so.

title: A changed record's wiki card shows its changes
statement: The wiki card of a record changed since the Changes baseline MUST show a Changes section: each changed field old → new, marked with the theme's tokens, and the links added and removed. An added record's card MUST say "New since <baseline>". The card's summary MUST say it in one line.

title: Every stage shows the same Changes controls
statement: The Graph, the ERD and the Trace MUST show the same Changes controls in one place, the shared stage toolbar, after Frame and before the stage's own controls (LA-PAT-APP-UX-R21), the first group to fold into its More menu when the toolbar is narrow: the Highlight changes toggle, the baseline picker, Follow, and the Changes panel's toggle with its count. Each toggle MUST say whether it is on, and each MUST have its command (Highlight changes g l, the Changes panel g d, Follow in the palette). Next change and Previous change MUST be commands too, bound to ] and [ and rebindable through Key bindings.

title: Every stage marks the changes, and Highlight changes makes them obvious
statement: As the data reloads, the Graph, the ERD and the Trace MUST mark what changed (LA-EXP-UC15-R02): an added record a soft glow and a "new" dot, a changed record a brief pulse in its own color then a lasting "changed" dot, a removed record a ghost outline fading over a few seconds; under reduced motion, the dots only. With Highlight changes on (LA-EXP-UC15-R03) they MUST instead draw, for every record changed from the baseline, a pill (New, Changed or Removed: text and color, readable at its box's size and left out below it by the level of detail), a thick outline in the change's color and a light tint; everything unchanged MUST dim to about 20% with the stages' one fade; a removed record MUST stay as a dashed ghost until Highlight changes is turned off; and every container MUST carry its roll-up (LA-EXP-UC15-R07). Nothing MUST be laid out again for a mark or for Highlight changes.

title: Every stage shows its key as a bar along the bottom
statement: Every stage (the Graph, the ERD and the Trace) MUST show its key as one frosted bar, always visible, along the bottom of the open space between the nav and the wiki card or the chat, on the camera's row: right of the camera's buttons and left of the minimap, never covering either. Each entry MUST be a small sample of what it explains (a swatch, a shape, a line) and one or two words, its whole meaning in its tooltip, and the bar MUST list only what the stage draws now: a kind the filters hide leaves it, the live marks only while there are any, the change marks' pills, outlines and dimming only while Highlight changes is on and the Trace's fade only while a path is lit. The bar MUST be a floating panel the open space measures (`data-floating`), so the camera frames above it, in the app's small UI text, readable in light and dark at AA contrast. Too long for one row it MUST wrap to as many rows as it needs, every entry whole, never cut at an edge or scrolled out of sight, at any width and whether the wiki card is open or collapsed. It MUST be one tab stop, a region named Key whose keys never walk the stage. On a phone it MUST be a Key chip at the foot of the stage that opens the entries, each with its meaning, as a sheet. On every stage the bar MUST end with what scroll does now, Scroll pans or, with Scroll to zoom on, Scroll zooms (`LA-V93-R07`), its tooltip naming every wheel move and where to change it; the phone's sheet leaves it out, a phone having no wheel. The stage toolbar MUST hold no Key.

title: Each tab has its own Back and Forward; the window's history follows the active tab
statement: In the desktop app each tab MUST keep its own history: a move MUST drop the tab's forward entries and add one, and Back and Forward (the title bar's buttons, Ctrl+- and Ctrl+Shift+-, and View › Tabs › Back and Forward on Cmd+[ and Cmd+]) MUST step through the active tab's history only, never into another tab's. Switching tabs MUST give the window the new tab's history, so the window's own Back and Forward step through it, and a reload MUST bring back every tab's history.
group_name: Explore several places at once in tabs

title: On the web, a browser tab is one place
statement: In the web app a browser tab MUST be one place, with no tab strip and no tab commands of the app's own: its focus and stage MUST be in the address, its history MUST be the browser's own, one entry per move, and its depth, kind filters and wiki card MUST be kept in session storage, which is the browser tab's own, and come back on a reload. Cmd or Ctrl+click and middle-click on a link (a real `href`) or on a box on the stage MUST open its address in a new browser tab.
group_name: Explore several places at once in tabs

title: Every part shows the page's one focus
statement: The stage, the header strip and the wiki card MUST always show the same record or group: the one the address names (the wiki card once the focus settles). Moving the center on the stage MUST change the address, and changing the address MUST move every part.

title: A page shows the stage the link names, or the place's
statement: When an address names a stage (`?stage=graph`, `?stage=erd`, `?stage=trace`) the page MUST open on it, and it becomes the remembered one; only an address without a stage MUST fall back to the place's stage, or for a space's first place the stage last chosen.
