Every page MUST show whichever stage it is asked for (`LA-PAT-APP-UX-R17`): no stage is dropped for the focus's kind.

title: Moving and tabs never change the session settings
statement: The session settings (the graph's layout, the minimap and the wiki card's width) MUST be one for the browser session, whatever the tab, place or page. Opening, activating, cycling or closing a tab, an arrow step, a click or Enter on a box, a link, and Back or Forward MUST NOT change them; only the person's own setting commands do.

title: Changes out of view are findable
statement: With Highlight changes on, every container on the Graph, the ERD and the Trace MUST show its roll-up and the nav MUST show the counts beside each domain, stage and folder (LA-EXP-UC15-R07); the minimap MUST mark each changed record and each edge of a stage MUST show a hint counting the changes past it, "4 changes →" (LA-EXP-UC15-R08); and Next change and Previous change MUST move the focus through the changed records, announced (LA-EXP-UC15-R09).

title: The products picker is the space chooser, over the last product's stage
statement: The products picker (`/`), the rail's home and the only page of its own outside every space, MUST be a card centered over the dimmed, out-of-reach stage of the last product the Reader was in (kept from one launch to the next), or over an empty map on a first launch. It MUST list each product as a card with its mark, name and domain count that opens the product where the Reader left it, wherever it is clicked, the last one marked, and nothing from inside the products: no problems and no coverage. Escape or a click on the dimmed stage MUST go back to that product, when there is one. On a phone it MUST be a sheet.

title: Trace works on every page
statement: Every page MUST offer the Trace stage, switched like the others and sitting after ERD, for any focus: a record a row shows stands on its box, its row selected, and any other record shows the product's rows.

title: A large trace stays fast
statement: The Trace stage MUST work out its rows once per product and data change and order them off the main thread, never per focus. Each frame MUST draw only what is in view, at most 260 boxes: boxes under 3 px tall or past the budget MUST be drawn as one bar per run with the selection's path marked on them; a box whose title would draw under 5 px MUST be a plain block. It MUST meet the big maps' budgets (LA-PLT-UC09-R13).

title: The trace's camera moves as the graph's
statement: The Trace stage's camera MUST take the graph's gestures from the one shared code, Scroll to zoom included (`LA-V93-R07`): a drag pans, the wheel pans or zooms as on the graph (scroll pans and Cmd or Ctrl with scroll zooms, or the other way round with Scroll to zoom on), a pinch zooms about the pointer, a gesture during a glide takes over from it, and . frames the focus again with a glide, as on the graph, its frame button carrying the key.

title: One row per use case, from outcome to suite
statement: The Trace stage MUST draw one row per use case of the product's space, each use case exactly once, across five columns, left to right: Outcome, Use case, Design flow, Technical flow and Acceptance test suite, read from the Trace read model (list-trace-rows, `LA-TRC-RM13`). The Outcome column MUST list each business outcome once, with a line to every use case whose capability serves it (a use case serving two outcomes has two lines into it); the rows and the outcomes MUST be ordered to keep those lines short, and the use cases serving no outcome MUST sit after the rest, under a dashed No outcome mark. Its key MUST name the rows, the stage colors drawn, the serves line, the path, a status, a gap, the toggle, the No outcome mark, the focus and what is faded.

title: A closed row shows a status per stage
statement: A closed row MUST show one box per stage: Design flow the interfaces its flow is carried out through and the requirements no step designs ("2 interfaces · all designed", "1 requirement not designed"), Technical flow its handlers and what is not built ("4 handlers · 1 not built"), Acceptance test suite its tests and what is not proved ("12 tests · all proved"); a stage with a gap (or no flow, handlers or tests) MUST be a dashed gap box.

title: Boxes open down to their children
statement: Each box with children MUST carry a toggle (▸, ▾ when open) that opens it down to its children, many boxes at once and each on its own; Expand row MUST open every stage of the focus's row, and Expand all one stage in every row (from the toolbar, or by a click on the column's name); what is open MUST be the place's (each tab its own). The use case MUST open to its UC requirements and the aggregates and read models its steps change and read; Design flow to its flow, and the flow to each interface's version of it (LA-V98-R23); Technical flow to the selected step's chain, from the parts of the views that present what it invokes to the operation or channel, the records that handle it, what reads and writes the data and where it is stored, with the connectors to its integrations (a hint when no step is selected; every step's chain grouped by step under Expand all); Acceptance test suite to "k of N proved", each UC requirement's use case tests and its flow's flow test, a dashed gap where proof is missing, and Lower tests, which opens to the tests of what they rest on (view and API requirements, invariants, storage requirements).

title: A selection draws its path across its row
statement: Selecting a box (a click, the walk, the address) MUST draw its path across its row, as lines from column to column, and light it, fading the rest: the requirement, the steps fulfilling it, their technical chain and the tests proving the requirement, back to the outcomes it serves; a box that is closed MUST stand in for what it holds, and a record several rows hold MUST light in each. Hovering a box MUST light its path while the pointer is on it. A click on a record MUST open it, keeping the stage, and the wiki card MUST follow the selection; a status, gap or hint opens nothing.

title: The Trace walk
statement: The stage walk MUST move Up and Down within a column as drawn, Left and Right along the row's links to the nearest linked box in the next column (else to the row's own box there), In opening a box and stepping to its first child, and Out stepping to the box it is in, or closing a cell's own box; from no box it MUST go to the first row's use case. Each step MUST be announced.

title: The Trace stage stays where it was
statement: The Trace stage MUST order its rows off the main thread, again only when its outcomes, rows or serves links change, keeping every row shown before at its slot until Tidy up (the stage's toolbar button and command, `t` by default): a removed row leaves a closed row's room, a new row takes such a room within three rows of where its links would put it, else goes at the end of its section; every outcome keeps its own place once placed, through opening rows and new data (a focused row's outcomes sit beside it only while it is focused, `LA-V98-R22`), a removed one leaves its place, and a new one takes the nearest free place within three boxes of the rows it serves, else the bottom of its column. It MUST lay its rows out top-down, every box one size, so that opening a box or a change inside a row moves only that row's boxes and the rows below it, which glide to their new places (`LA-PAT-APP-UX-R22`), and adding or removing a use case moves no other row; the camera stays where it is unless the focus's own box moved. It MUST draw only what is in view, as bars past the budget, and blocks below readable size (`LA-PLT-UC09-R13`).

title: The Trace stage as a list
statement: The canvas MUST be hidden from assistive technology, with a list under it as its accessible layer; on a phone the Trace stage MUST draw no canvas but that list: one use case at a time, picked from the rows in their order (the focus's row first), its outcomes and its four stages stacked down, each box with children carrying its own Open or Close button, the same boxes open as on the canvas.

title: The focused row's outcomes slide beside it
statement: While a row of the Trace stage is focused (any box in it, or its use case), the outcomes its use case serves MUST slide vertically to the row, stacked a box apart in their column's order and centered on the row's first line (never above the top of the view); every other outcome MUST keep its own place unless the stack covers it, when it steps aside, up or down, just enough; no other box moves. As the focus walks from row to row they MUST follow it, gliding like the rest of the stage (`LA-PAT-APP-UX-R22`), the lines from other rows to them following; focusing an outcome beside its row MUST leave it there; with no row focused every outcome MUST glide back to its own place (`LA-V98-R20`). Framing a focus in a row MUST include its outcomes when they fit, from the Outcome column on, its focused box whole on screen.

title: The Design flow opens each interface's version of the flow
statement: The Design flow MUST open to the use case's flow, and the flow to one box per interface that offers its use case, by ID, each opening that interface's version: its steps without the other interfaces' variants, each with the views (and their view requirements), the calls (and their API requirements) or the product's own records it is carried out in, and a dashed gap for a step the interface cannot reach. A flow no interface offers MUST open to its steps as written.

title: The chat floats at the right; the stage frames its focus beside it
statement: The chat MUST float at the right of the window as a frosted panel the stage measures, resizable and hidden from the title bar, its key or its own button, its open state and width kept in the session setting, and the page's other panels MUST keep clear of it. It MUST never collapse for space: the wiki card and then the nav give way to it instead (`LA-PAT-APP-UX-R18`).

title: The chat works by keyboard
statement: The Owner MUST be able to focus the chat's message box by its key, send with Enter, stop with Escape, walk the messages with the arrow keys, Home and End, and answer a permission prompt, all without a pointer.

title: The head shows the tools, the mode and Bypass; the empty chat says why not
statement: The chat MUST show, under its head, how many Lathe tools the session has and from which Lathe (or that they are loading, or did not load), and the permission mode as one control that opens a menu of the five, each with what it lets Claude do, chosen by keyboard or pointer; Bypass MUST ask first with a clear warning and show a badge in the head while on; the empty chat MUST say when Claude Code is not found (with where to install it) or not signed in (with `/login`), and start no session then.

title: The mic, what the chat hears, and the Voice menu
statement: Where the Mac recognizes speech on-device, the message box MUST have a mic button (pressed while dictating, its key shown) and, above it, a line saying what the chat hears (waiting for the wake phrase, dictating with how to send, or Quick mode's countdown, also drawn on Send); the head MUST have a Voice menu with voice activation, Quick mode and the phrases; and before macOS first asks for the microphone, the chat MUST say that audio never leaves the Mac. Elsewhere none of them MUST show.

title: The chat panel holds the picker, the queue, the chips, the images and the review
statement: The chat's head MUST have a model and effort picker beside the mode, and above the message box the panel MUST show, when there are any, the review bar of a turn under review, the queue of waiting messages, the chips of the records pointed at, the thumbnails of the images attached and, while a slash is typed, the list of skills; each turn that changed records MUST offer Review and Undo.
